mapData.title: NOETHER: A Constructive Framework for Metamorphic Pattern Discovery from Operator Algebras
mapData.abstract_summary: The paper studies metamorphic-relation (MR) identification (not MR fault-revealing effectiveness), asking whether a structured, operator-algebraic method can derive a broader and more explainable MR class / MetaPattern design space than expert MR sets and search-based MR generation by making each MR's algebraic origin and applicability boundary explicit. It introduces NOETHER, a two-level framework: an upstream layer that curates a program-family operator algebra and decomposes it into eight recurrent operator blocks (symmetry, order, self-adjointness, time reversal, limits, qualitative dynamics, method comparison, relational equivalence), and a downstream CONSTRUCT-MP layer that derives MetaPatterns/MR classes from those blocks and checks whether a program interface exposes the inputs/observations needed to instantiate an executable MR. Evidence is organized along three axes: binary operator-block coverage of expert MR sets vs NOETHER, an origin/boundary/redundancy/readability comparison against search-based generation, and cross-domain derivation traces across program families; mutation and head-to-head results are retained only as secondary executability/sanity-check evidence. The stated conclusion is that NOETHER is a theory-guided MR-identification framework that derives MR classes from governing-equation operator algebra, makes their origin and boundary auditable, and exposes structural MR design-space coverage not explicit in expert or search-generated MR sets.
contributions: C1: NOETHER, a layered MR-class / MetaPattern identification framework combining an empirically curated structural decomposition (upstream, Hypothesis 1, partly distilled from the authors' prior PWR MR catalogue) with a constructive algorithm (CONSTRUCT-MP, downstream) deriving MetaPatterns from a program-induced operator algebra.

C2a (positive theory): Theorem 1 proves a no-drop closure invariant under the Translate operator over the algebra-induced MR space MR(A_P); Theorem 2 gives polynomial-time decidability of CONSTRUCT-MP under a finite generating set. Explicitly framed as a modest well-formedness / by-construction guarantee, not fault-detection superiority.

C2b (negative theory): The stronger absolute-completeness conjecture (Theorem 1' / Conjecture, over arbitrary properties expressible in A_P) is FALSE on A_PWR, shown via two PWR safety MRs (non-additivity of rod-bank reactivity worth; second-order mixed dependence of k_eff on moderator temperature and boron concentration); these identify five pairwise-independent structural obstructions in Translate's signature, plus five further candidate dimensions surveyed on A_equi and A_rel (ten Translate-extension dimensions total).

C2c (limiting theory): The Invariance-Blindness Theorem (Theorem 3 / thm:ibt) for the symmetry (G) and self-adjoint (T*) blocks: an algebra-derived MR's detection kernel equals exactly the structure-preserving faults, within the linear operator-implementation fault class and under a faithfulness condition attainable by a finite test. Corollaries: single-block batteries are incomplete; completeness needs oracle families with trivial joint kernel; a cross-implementation differential oracle is the complementary (common-mode) oracle.

C3: Instantiation on a real-world program family (reactor physics) that systematises and re-classifies the prior inductive catalogue: reproduces three prior MetaPatterns (P1->m_inv, P2->m_mono, P3->m_conv), refines two (P4->m_dyn, P5->m_cmp), and de-duplicates/predicts two (m_adj adjoint reciprocity, m_rev collisionless reversibility); deflationary (over-counting) direction demonstrated on three independent cases (a sorting library; Murphy et al. 2008's six ML MR classes re-decoded; the reactor catalogue itself).

C4: Structural transferability at the algebra-skeleton level (not cross-domain empirical superiority) via instantiation on three structurally distinct operator algebras at differentiated depth: Boltzmann reactor-physics transport, equivariant ML, and relational query optimisers (the last exercising the relational-equivalence block beyond the Lie-group / self-adjoint / time-reversal core).

C5: An evidence protocol for MR identification: binary expert-vs-NOETHER operator-block coverage, search-vs-NOETHER origin/boundary comparison, and compact cross-domain derivation traces, with mutation/GenMorph/DeepCrime-style results treated as secondary executability checks rather than evidence of average fault-detection superiority.

key_claims.claim: There is an 'origin-closure-transferability gap': existing MetaPattern catalogues are induced from observed examples and cannot answer why these patterns, under what closure conditions, and how they transfer across program families.

Theorem 1 converts an empirical-adequacy claim ('our grid covers X% of observed MRs') into a structural-adequacy claim ('exhaustive of the Translate-reachable algebra-induced MR space, modulo explicit out-of-scope classes'); closure is by-construction within Definition def:alg-induced's scope.

Absolute completeness (Theorem 1') is false on the PWR core diffusion algebra A_PWR via two regulatory-essential safety MRs, identifying five pairwise-independent obstructions in Translate's signature (independence proved by per-block exhaustion).

Invariance-Blindness Theorem: for the G and T* blocks an algebra-derived MR's detection kernel equals exactly the structure-preserving (equivariant / self-adjoint-compatible) faults, within the linear operator-implementation fault class; a finite faithful test attains this (non-tautological tightness from finite fault-dimensionality).
key_claims.section: Section 3.4 / subsec:ibt (theory/ibt_section_3_4.tex, Theorem thm:ibt + Lemma lem:reachability)

key_claims.claim: On binary operator-block coverage, expert industrial corpora (SACOS/SPARK/LOCUST) cover only the O_le block, whereas NOETHER's derivation protocol covers six operator blocks on held-out numerical libraries (numpy.linalg, numpy.fft).

NOETHER re-classifies the prior reactor-physics inductive catalogue: reproduces three patterns, refines two (exposing conflations), and predicts two structurally distinct classes (m_adj, m_rev); these are systematisation, not de novo discovery, with an acknowledged circularity caveat for the 'prediction'.

In the equivariant-ML secondary case study, Set N (NOETHER) achieves detection 7/20 and structural coverage 1.00 with 5 unique detections, vs Set L (LLM) 2/20 / 0.40 and Set B (literature) 0/20 / 0.20; cat-(iv) gradient-reversal is 5/5 for Set N only. This is explicitly construct-validity-controlled, not averaged superiority.
The L*-block blindness prediction is confirmed: the L_scale MR kills only 2 of 44 PIT mutants on the six L*-admitting Java SUTs, a falsifiable ex-ante structural prediction.

In the head-to-head at GenMorph's published 30-min budget, Set N is DOMINATED by GenMorph's Set G in aggregate on the algebra-disrupting D1 stratum (pooled McNemar p=0.0043, n=62, underpowered); the framework's claimed contribution is per-block derivability, structural coverage extension, and an ex-ante D2 <=10% kill-rate prediction (held at 2/29=6.9%), not detection superiority.

The DeepCrime-style real-fault pilot is explicitly underpowered (n=5): Set N 2/5, Set L 0/5, Set B 0/5; cat-v-02/04/05 detected by no MR set, flagged as the pilot's principal negative finding for Hypothesis 1 (candidate parameter-distribution-divergence ninth block).

Induction is relocated, not eliminated: the upstream distillation of A_P remains a human/empirical task (Hypothesis 1) with six documented out-of-scope candidate-ninth-block families and four domain-level out-of-scope classes; only the downstream A_P -> M(A_P) step is mechanical and provable.

structure: Section 1: Introduction - Noether-theorem analogy, MT/MR identification bottleneck, the origin-closure-transferability gap, framework overview (Fig. 1 architecture), five MR-identification contributions C1-C5, Scope of contribution + 'Boundary of contribution' boxes

Section 2: Related Work - (2.1) MT and the MR identification bottleneck; (2.2) Structured MR identification (METRIC/METRIC+ etc.); (2.3) Automated MR identification (mining/search/LLM); (2.4) MetaPattern catalogues and empirical adequacy (Ying et al. family trees, PMCM); (2.5) Convergent diagnosis; plus paragraphs on the separate minimum-complete-MR-subset line and on head-to-head comparator selection

Section 3: Proposed Method - counting rule; (3.1) Operator-algebraic preliminaries with building blocks B1-B8, Hypothesis 1, out-of-scope remarks; (3.2) Deriving MR classes with CONSTRUCT-MP (block invariant, Translate, algebra-induced MR, Steps 1-4, Theorem 1 closure, Theorem 2 decidability, complexity table); (3.3 = subsec:ibt via \input theory/ibt_section_3_4) Invariance-Blindness Theorem; Boltzmann instantiation (reactor physics, prior-catalogue refinement, Noether-style m_adj derivation); Cross-domain equivariant-ML instantiation; A third domain: relational query optimisers; A negative instantiation: PWR core simulators (two propositions falsifying Theorem 1')
Section 4: Experiments - evidence protocol; EQ1 expert MR set coverage; EQ2 search-based comparison; EQ3 cross-domain operator-block sharing; secondary executability checks

Section 5: Results and Discussion - reading guide; (5.1) Primary MR-identification evidence (3 tables for EQ1-EQ3); (5.2) Secondary executability check: equivariant-ML case study (Sets N/L/B, 20-mutation set, pre-registered H1/H2, DeepCrime-style n=5 pilot); empirical test of decomposition (L*-block blindness on Java SUTs, PIT, test design, central result, head-to-head Set N vs Set G); Relationship with METRIC/METRIC+; Reassessing PMCM coverage (worked example); Empirical evidence for the Invariance-Blindness Theorem
Section 6: Threats to Validity and Limitations - validity framework; limitations beyond validity
Section 7: Future Work - practical engineering guidance; the remaining human role and partial automation of A_P distillation
Section 9: Data and Artifact Availability - Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20250634, supplementary S1-S4 manifest, artefact badges

research_questions: EQ1 (expert MR set coverage): Can NOETHER derive MR classes in operator blocks absent from expert MR sets? Answered by binary operator-block coverage using SACOS/SPARK/LOCUST and reactor-physics corpora.

EQ2 (search-based comparison): How does NOETHER differ from search-based MR generation in origin explanation, boundary explanation, redundancy/readability, and maintenance? GenMorph and related generated-test/oracle work used as complementary comparators.

EQ3 (cross-domain operator-block sharing): Can the same operator block explain MR classes across different program families, domains, or solvers? Answered through compact derivation traces (Boltzmann/reactor physics, equivariant ML, relational query optimisers, held-out numerical libraries).
Pre-registered case-study H1 (coverage): coverage_NOETHER(N)=1.0 by construction while coverage of LLM set L and literature set B are strictly < 1.0.
Pre-registered case-study H2 (unique detection): Set N has at least one uniquely-detected mutation, in category (iv) gradient-reversal sign error, via rho_train-rev.

Implicit cross-cutting question framed in Section 1: the origin-closure-transferability gap - the structural source of MetaPatterns, the closure conditions on a discovered MP set, and how MP sets transfer when the program family changes.
mapData.empirical_setup: PUTs/SUTs across three substrates. (1) Equivariant-ML case study: a single E(3)-equivariant graph neural network (EGNN, 2 layers, hidden dim 16, 5,189 params) as a minimal stand-in for an SE(3)-Transformer, trained on a 5-class procedural point-cloud dataset (sphere/cube/torus/cone/helix; 64 pts/cloud; 400 train/100 val; rotation augmentation; 25 epochs; val acc 0.93). Mutation set = 20 defects in four categories x5 (wrong-sign loss; equivariance break; precision degradation; gradient-reversal sign error). Plus a DeepCrime-style n=5 real-fault pilot (cat-v-01..05). (2) Java algebra-rich substrate: 10 SUTs from Apache Commons Math (midpoint, exactLog2, isSequence, clamp, signum, ComplexSignal.add, gcdSig, lcmSig, hypotSig, powerSig); six admit an L_scale MR; PIT 1.7.4 default mutators, JUnit codegen + 2-pass surefire green-suite filter; pre-registered SUT criterion (configs/d4j_algebra_rich_criterion.json) on branch feat/d4j-algebra-rich; central L*-blindness test denominator 44 mutants; head-to-head pooled n=62 mutants. (3) Reactor physics / PWR: authors' own prior PWR-MR corpus (supplementary S2) distilled from Bell&Glasstone and Lewis&Miller; 12-MR element-wise table (7 representative shown); independent 18-MR LLM-panel audit (Fleiss kappa=0.857, 3 raters, 4 categories); negative-instantiation algebra A_PWR (PARCS/SIMULATE-3/5/ANC/SMART family). (4) Relational query optimisers: A_rel with four derived MRs cross-corroborated against QED/SPES query-equivalence literature. MR sets: Set N (NOETHER-derived, 5 in case study / 30 in Java study), Set L (GPT-4 LLM-prompt baseline, also a 2-vendor x 5-temperature ensemble Set L), Set B (literature MT-for-ML baseline). Baselines/comparators: Set G = GenMorph GP-evolved MRs at the published 30-min GAssert budget (the single executable head-to-head, with a 1-min sensitivity rerun); METRIC+ contrasted as a category-enumeration scaffold (PIT-based comparison committed as future work S4); MR-Scout omitted (mining input structurally absent); AutoMT/GPTMR noted as out-of-substrate. Datasets/expert corpora named: SACOS/SPARK/LOCUST (supplementary S11), held-out numpy.linalg / numpy.fft (S12), Murphy et al. 2008 six ML MR classes, Segura et al. IMDb subset, TPC-H-class queries. Statistics reported: McNemar exact, Fisher exact, Wilson 95% CIs, Holm-Bonferroni; small samples explicitly flagged underpowered. Artifacts archived on Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20250634.

guide.venue: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology (TOSEM)

requirements.requirement: Manuscripts must be prepared using ACM guidelines and templates for electronic submission (the acmart LaTeX document class or the ACM Word template). TOSEM is an ACM journal, so the journal trim is acmsmall: e.g. \documentclass[acmsmall,review,manuscript,screen]{acmart}.

For peer review the submission must be single-column. Add the 'manuscript' option (\documentclass[manuscript]{acmart} / acmsmall,manuscript) which generates single-column review format. ACM production reformats accepted manuscripts into the final journal layout, so authors do NOT submit in the final double-column production layout.

Desk-reject trigger: a manuscript that is 'incomplete, over the page limit, or incorrectly formatted' may be returned without review. Ensure the file is complete and uses the correct acmart class/options before submission.

TOSEM uses a SINGLE-blind review process for regular submissions: the EIC assigns each paper to a committee member (associate editor) who selects three reviewers for regular papers and two reviewers for position papers; reviewer identities are anonymous to authors, but author identities are NOT hidden from reviewers. Authors therefore do NOT anonymize regular TOSEM submissions by default. (Note: some special tracks/CFPs differ — verify the specific track's CFP.)

If a track or special section does require double-anonymous review, use the acmart 'anonymous,review' options (\documentclass[acmsmall,anonymous,review]{acmart}), which anonymize the work and add line numbers; remove author info, acknowledgments, and any citations/related-work discussion that reveals authorship. Confirm the requirement against the specific track CFP before anonymizing.

Soft length cap for regular submissions: 'Extremely long submissions -- as a general rule, those that exceed approximately 11,000 words -- may be returned without review at the discretion of the editor-in-chief.' There is no fixed hard page limit for regular research papers, but exceeding ~11,000 words risks return without review.

Track-specific limits: Journal-first / fast-impact track papers must be no more than 45 TOSEM pages of text (excluding bibliography) to qualify for upgrade to the fast-impact track; position papers must not exceed 4 pages excluding bibliography. Verify the limit for the exact submission type chosen.

An acceptable paper must contain: (a) motivation and clear objectives; (b) demonstration of novelty and superiority compared to related work; (c) evidence of effectiveness, reproducibility, scalability, and practical relevance. The desk editor screens for these elements.

TOSEM 'publishes original, significant, reproducible and archival results in all areas of software engineering research.' Submissions must be original (not previously published and not under consideration elsewhere — a statement to this effect is required at submission) and must clear a significance + reproducibility + archival bar.

An abstract is required (acmart \begin{abstract}...\end{abstract}); it should be concise and summarize the work. acmart does not impose a hard word count, but the abstract must be self-contained (no internal cross-references). No formal structured-abstract requirement is imposed by TOSEM/acmart.

CCS (ACM Computing Classification System) concepts AND author-defined keywords are REQUIRED for all articles over two pages in length (optional only for one/two-page articles). Generate CCS concepts via the ACM CCS tool (https://dl.acm.org/ccs/ccs.cfm) and paste the generated \ccsdesc and \keywords code into the manuscript. Providing proper CCS indexing is explicitly described as an important part of preparing the paper.

References must use the ACM Reference Format: \bibliographystyle{ACM-Reference-Format} with a BibTeX .bib file. Required for all articles over one page. Authors' names must be complete — use full first names (e.g., 'Donald E. Knuth'), not initials. Include DOIs where available.

ACM/TOSEM uses the ORCID identification system: if a submitting author does not already have an ORCID when uploading a new submission to ManuscriptCentral, they will be asked to obtain one. ACM is committed to collecting ORCID iDs from all published authors.

TOSEM encourages Replicated Computational Results (RCR) Reports that complement papers with information supporting replication. An RCR report must be titled '[Paper Title] – RCR Report', provide a link to artifacts on a long-term archival platform that complies with FAIR principles, and include the artifact DOI. RCR reports are published in a dedicated TOSEM section.

Artifacts are assessed under the standard ACM Artifact Review and Badging policy. Authors may apply for badges: 'Artifact Available', 'Artifact Evaluated – Functional', and 'Results Reproduced'. Artifacts are evaluated on whether they are documented, consistent, complete, exercisable, and include appropriate evidence of verification and validation. The artifact package must document how to (i) obtain, (ii) unpack, (iii) get started with, and (iv) use the artifacts.

ACM Publications Policy on Research Involving Human Participants and Subjects applies: studies involving human participants must comply with the policy (ethics/IRB-equivalent review and reporting). Authors must adhere to this policy as part of ACM submission requirements.

ACM Generative-AI policy applies: generative AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT) may NOT be listed as authors; use of generative AI to create content is permitted but must be fully disclosed in the work. Disclose any GenAI assistance.

At submission the lead author must create a ManuscriptCentral account with full contact information and provide a statement that the material has not been previously published and is not currently under consideration elsewhere.
Submissions are made electronically through the TOSEM ManuscriptCentral portal at http://mc.manuscriptcentral.com/tosem.

research.angle: Metamorphic-testing meta-patterns and MR classification/taxonomy: is a "meta-pattern" abstraction layer ABOVE concrete MR patterns genuinely novel, or already covered by existing MR taxonomies/pattern catalogues? Verdict: the abstraction LAYER itself is NOT new (MRPs-as-templates, MRP family trees, symmetry-based MRPs, query-based MRPs, and the Murphy ML MR categories all predate this). What is novel on this angle is the GROUNDING of that layer: NOETHER replaces inductive curation of patterns with a constructive derivation of MetaPatterns from a program-induced operator algebra (Translate: block invariant -> executable MR), plus positive/negative/limiting theory (closure, decidability, falsified absolute-completeness, Invariance-Blindness). No prior MT work derives the meta-pattern layer algebraically or proves closure/decidability/blindness over it. So the contribution is the algebraic constructive engine + de-duplication/over-counting direction, not the "abstraction above patterns" idea per se.

closest_prior_works.cite: Ying, Towey, Bellotti, Chua, Zhou — Metamorphic Relation Patterns for Metamorphic Testing, Exploration and Robustness
closest_prior_works.relation: CLOSEST competitor on the exact angle. Explicitly defines MRPs as 'abstractions or templates for multiple concrete MRs', gives formal definitions to CLASSIFY MRPs, identifies new MRPs, and proposes 'MRP family trees' to organize prior+new MRPs for reuse/reference/inference. This IS the meta-pattern abstraction layer above concrete MRs. Difference: Ying's classification is inductive/taxonomic (organize already-discovered patterns into trees); NOETHER's layer is constructive/generative (derive the MetaPattern set mechanically from an operator algebra via Translate) with closure + decidability theorems and a falsified completeness conjecture. NOETHER already cites it (Ying2025MRPatterns). The novelty rests on construction+proof, NOT on the abstraction layer, which Ying already established.

closest_prior_works.cite: Segura, Durán, Troya, Ruiz-Cortés — Metamorphic Relation Patterns for Query-Based Systems
closest_prior_works.venue_year: MET@ICSE 2019 (+ ACM MET 2022 automated generation follow-up)
closest_prior_works.relation: Introduced MRPs as reusable, domain-spanning templates from which concrete MRs are instantiated, and later AUTOMATED generation of MRs from those patterns for a whole class of systems. Direct prior art for 'a pattern layer above concrete MRs that can be mechanically instantiated.' NOETHER generalizes the instantiation idea from one domain (query systems) to a domain-parametric algebraic skeleton with proofs. Cited (Segura2019QBSMRPatterns / Segura2022QBSAutoMR).

closest_prior_works.cite: Zhou, Sun, Chen, Towey — Metamorphic Relations for Enhancing System Understanding and Use
closest_prior_works.relation: Develops MRs/MRPs including symmetry-style relations and metamorphic exploration; part of the lineage that frames recurrent mathematical structures (symmetry, periodicity) as pattern sources. NOETHER's symmetry (G) block and several MetaPatterns overlap conceptually with this symmetry-MRP work; the delta is formalizing such structures as operator-algebra blocks plus the Invariance-Blindness Theorem on the G/T* blocks. Cited (Zhou2020SymmetryMRP).

closest_prior_works.cite: Chen, Poon, Xie — METRIC: Metamorphic Relation Identification based on the Category-Choice framework (and Sun et al. METRIC+ 2021)
closest_prior_works.relation: The canonical STRUCTURED/systematic MR identification framework — a manual-but-systematic procedure for enumerating MRs from input (and input+output) categories. This is the strongest 'structured framework' baseline NOETHER positions against (it claims to be deductive where METRIC is a heuristic enumeration). Same identification-framework genre, different epistemics (category enumeration vs algebraic construction). Cited (ChenMETRIC2016, SunMETRICplus2021).

closest_prior_works.cite: Murphy, Kaiser, Hu, Wu — Properties of Machine Learning Applications for Use in Metamorphic Testing
closest_prior_works.relation: The original taxonomy of six general MR CLASSES for ML (additive, multiplicative, permutative, invertive, inclusive, exclusive). This is an early concrete-class taxonomy — a meta-pattern catalogue avant la lettre. NOETHER explicitly re-decodes these six classes as a deflationary/over-counting demonstration (C3), so it is both prior art and a worked example. Cited (Murphy2008).

closest_prior_works.cite: Segura, Fraser, Sanchez, Ruiz-Cortés — A Survey on Metamorphic Testing; and Chen, Kuo, Liu, Poon, Towey, Tse, Zhou — Metamorphic Testing (ACM CSUR 2018)
closest_prior_works.relation: The two field-defining surveys; both already classify MRs and survey MR identification. Establish that 'MR classification' as an activity is mature. NOETHER must (and does) distinguish its contribution from survey-level taxonomy. Survey cited (Segura2016); the Chen et al. CSUR survey itself does not appear in the visible bib keys and would strengthen the related-work framing.

closest_prior_works.cite: Li, Liu, Poon, Towey, Sun, Zheng, Zhou, Chen — Metamorphic Relation Generation: State of the Art and Research Directions
closest_prior_works.relation: Most recent survey of MR generation/identification approaches (structured frameworks, mining, search/evolutionary, LLM). It is the framing reference NOETHER uses to assert the 'shared inductive grounding' gap (origin/closure/transferability). Sets the bar at the target venue (TOSEM) and confirms no existing approach offers a constructive algebraic derivation with closure/decidability proofs. Cited (LiTOSEM2025).

closest_prior_works.cite: Kanewala, Bieman, Ben-Hur — Predicting metamorphic relations for testing scientific software (graph kernels)
closest_prior_works.relation: Leading ML-based MR prediction line: predicts which of a FIXED predefined MR set applies to a program. Relevant because it presupposes a finite catalogue of MR types (a de facto meta-pattern set) and learns the program->pattern mapping inductively. NOETHER derives that catalogue per-domain instead of fixing it a priori. Cited (Kanewala2016GraphKernel).

genuinely_novel: Constructive (by-construction) derivation of the meta-pattern layer from a program-induced operator algebra A_P via the Translate operator (block invariant -> executable MR) — relocating induction from per-program MR sampling to a per-domain algebraic curation step. No prior MT work derives MetaPatterns algebraically; existing MRP/taxonomy work (Ying 2025, Segura 2019, Zhou 2020, Murphy 2008) is inductive/taxonomic.

Positive theory on the meta-pattern layer: Theorem 1 (algebraic closure under Translate — every MR maps to a unique MetaPattern under a canonical block ordering) and Theorem 2 (polynomial-time decidability of CONSTRUCT-MP under a finite generating set). MT literature has surveys and adequacy criteria (Fu 2024) but no closure/decidability theorems over an MR-generating algebra.

Negative theory: explicit refutation of an absolute-completeness conjecture (Theorem 1') on the PWR algebra via two genuine domain counterexamples (non-additivity of rod-bank reactivity worth; second-order mixed k_eff dependence on moderator temperature and boron concentration), yielding five pairwise-independent structural obstructions in Translate's signature plus five surveyed extension dimensions. A falsified-completeness result for a constructive MR framework is new to MT.

Limiting theory: the Invariance-Blindness Theorem (Theorem 3) characterizing an algebra-derived MR's detection kernel = the commutant/structure-preserving faults within a linear fault class under a finite-attainable faithfulness condition, with corollaries (single-block batteries incomplete; completeness needs trivial joint kernel; differential cross-implementation oracle is the complementary common-mode oracle). This connects MR detection power to operator-theoretic kernels — a formal blind-spot characterization absent from prior MR-pattern work.

Deflationary / over-counting direction: using the algebra to DE-DUPLICATE and predict redundancy among published patterns (sorting library; Murphy 2008's six ML classes re-decoded; the reactor catalogue itself). Prior taxonomy work organizes/expands catalogues; using a generative theory to argue prior catalogues over-count is a distinct, falsifiable claim.

Domain-parametric transferability at the algebra-skeleton level demonstrated on three structurally distinct algebras (Boltzmann transport, equivariant ML, relational query optimisers), exercising blocks beyond the symmetry/self-adjoint/time-reversal core (relational-equivalence block). This is structural rather than empirical-superiority transfer — a different and more defensible novelty claim than cross-domain fault-detection wins.
incremental_or_overlapping: The core idea of a 'meta-pattern / MRP abstraction layer above concrete MRs' is NOT novel: Ying et al. 2025 (STVR) already define MRPs as templates, formally classify them, and build MRP family trees for reuse/reference/inference; Segura et al. 2019 already use MRPs as instantiable templates. The manuscript must (and largely does) frame its delta as construction+proof, not as inventing the layer.

The eight recurrent mathematical structures used as blocks (symmetry, order/monotonicity, self-adjointness, time-reversal, limits, qualitative dynamics, method-comparison, relational equivalence) are individually well-known MR sources scattered across prior work (symmetry/periodicity in Zhou 2020; additive/multiplicative/permutative in Murphy 2008; equality/inequality numerical MRs in Zhang 2014 / AutoMR 2019). Packaging them as a decomposition is organizational; the novelty is the algebraic closure/Translate machinery, not the block list, which is an empirical hypothesis (Hypothesis 1) by the authors' own framing.

The reactor-physics instantiation systematises the authors' OWN prior PWR MR catalogue (Wang/Yang/Li/Liu/Yan 2022 input/output-pattern separation; Zhang et al. 2023 composition-layer study). The 'reproduces three / refines two / de-duplicates two' result is partly self-referential reorganization, so its evidential weight as independent validation is limited — closer to a retrospective rationalization of prior inductive findings.

Polynomial-time decidability (Theorem 2) is conditioned on 'a finite generating set' — a strong assumption that does much of the work; absent a method to obtain a finite generating set in general, the decidability result is a well-formedness guarantee rather than a practical identification guarantee (the manuscript concedes this as a 'modest by-construction' claim, which is honest but bounds the contribution).

The executability/fault-detection evidence (mutation/GenMorph/DeepCrime-style) is explicitly demoted to secondary checks. On the pure empirical-effectiveness axis the paper does not advance SOTA, so any reviewer expecting fault-detection superiority over METRIC/Ying/LLM-based generation will find the empirical layer thin by design.

research.academic_level_verdict: TOSEM-worthy on this angle, conditionally. The 'meta-pattern abstraction layer' framing alone is NOT novel — Ying et al. 2025 (STVR), Segura et al. 2019, Zhou et al. 2020, and Murphy et al. 2008 already established that a pattern/class layer sits above concrete MRs, and the most recent TOSEM survey (Li et al. 2025) shows MR classification is a mature activity. What lifts this to TOSEM level is the CONSTRUCTIVE + THEOREM-BACKED treatment of that layer: deriving MetaPatterns from a program-induced operator algebra (Translate), proving closure and decidability, FALSIFYING an absolute-completeness conjecture with genuine domain counterexamples, and characterizing detection blind spots via an Invariance-Blindness Theorem. That positive/negative/limiting theory package is, to the best of the searched literature, without precedent in MT — no prior SE/MT work derives the MR-pattern layer algebraically or proves closure/decidability/blindness over it (group-theoretic/operator results in the corpus are confined to equivariant-ML/physics, not MR derivation). The contribution is genuinely theoretical and falsifiable, matching TOSEM's appetite for foundational, well-formed results. The principal risks a reviewer will press: (1) the empirical layer is deliberately secondary (no fault-detection SOTA claim), so the paper lives or dies on the theory's depth and the honesty of its scope; (2) the flagship reactor instantiation re-organizes the authors' OWN prior catalogue, weakening it as independent validation; (3) Theorem 2's decidability hinges on an assumed finite generating set; (4) the related-work section must very sharply separate 'we invented an abstraction layer' (false) from 'we give the first constructive algebraic generator + closure/completeness/blindness theory for that layer' (true and defensible). If the manuscript foregrounds the construction-and-proof delta over Ying/Segura/Zhou and tones down any implication that the abstraction layer itself is new, the angle clears the TOSEM novelty bar.

research.angle: The test-oracle problem under a symmetry / invariance / group-theoretic framing of metamorphic relations: does NOETHER's claim — that MRs can be derived constructively from a program-induced operator algebra A_P (symmetry group G, self-adjoint T*, time-reversal, Lie-group/equivariance, relational-equivalence blocks), with closure/decidability theorems and an Invariance-Blindness theorem bounding the detection kernel to the commutant of structure-preserving faults — have published precedent, and how close? Verdict: treating MRs as symmetries/invariants is widespread and old; the EXPLICIT operator-algebra + Noether-style invariance + commutant/fault-kernel completeness formalism applied to MR identification is, to the extent the SE literature is indexed, not previously published. The novelty is in the formal apparatus and the negative/limiting theory, not in the symmetry intuition itself.

closest_prior_works.cite: Gotlieb & Botella, Automated metamorphic testing / Gotlieb, Exploiting symmetries to test programs (Symmetric Testing)
closest_prior_works.relation: CLOSEST prior art on the angle. Symmetric Testing is the original explicit symmetry/permutation-group framing of oracle-free testing: user-defined symmetry properties (a special case of MRs restricted to permutation/symmetry relations) drive automatic test generation + symmetry checking. NOETHER generalizes this from permutation symmetries to a full operator algebra (group G PLUS monotone, linear, self-adjoint, time-reversal, limit, Lie-equivariance, relational-equivalence blocks) and adds constructive derivation + completeness/limiting theorems. If NOETHER does not cite and position against Symmetric Testing, that is a publication-blocking omission: a TOSEM reviewer will read NOETHER's G-block as a strict superset of Symmetric Testing.

closest_prior_works.cite: Patel & Hierons, A mapping study on testing non-testable systems
closest_prior_works.relation: Explicitly states that some refer to MT as Symmetric Testing when only permutation relations are used (Gotlieb 2003). Directly documents that the symmetry-group reading of MRs is already named and surveyed. Strengthens the requirement that NOETHER position against the symmetry-as-MR lineage rather than presenting group-theoretic MRs as new.

closest_prior_works.cite: Segura, Fraser, Sanchez & Ruiz-Cortes, A Survey on Metamorphic Testing
closest_prior_works.relation: Canonical MT survey (532+ citations). Catalogs how MRs are identified and the recurring symmetry/permutation/additivity/equality relation patterns. NOETHER's eight building blocks largely re-organize relation families already enumerated descriptively here, but Segura provides no algebraic-structure / closure / decidability theory. Baseline NOETHER must show it advances beyond; almost certainly a required citation.

closest_prior_works.cite: Segura, Duran, Troya & Ruiz-Cortes, A Template-Based Approach to Describing Metamorphic Relations
closest_prior_works.relation: Closest prior attempt to give MRs a structured, reusable schema (input/output relation templates). NOETHER's MetaPattern/Translate apparatus is a more formal (algebra-induced) descendant of this structured-MR-description goal. Overlaps on motivation (systematizing/de-duplicating MRs); differs by providing a generative algebra rather than a documentation template.

closest_prior_works.cite: Qiu, Zheng, Chen & Poon, Theoretical and Empirical Analyses of the Effectiveness of Metamorphic Relation Composition
closest_prior_works.relation: Most formal prior treatment of MR algebraic structure in mainstream MT: composition of MRs and conditions for fault-detection preservation under composition. Nearest thing to an algebra of MRs before NOETHER, but studies composition of given MRs, not derivation of MRs from a program-induced operator algebra, and has no Noether/commutant/closure-under-named-operator theory. Overlap on the MRs-form-a-composable-structure idea; NOETHER goes further with closure under Translate + canonical ordering.

closest_prior_works.cite: Liu, Liu & Chen, A New Method for Constructing Metamorphic Relations
closest_prior_works.relation: Foundational on systematic MR construction (composing simple MRs into richer ones). Establishes the constructive-MR-generation problem NOETHER's CONSTRUCT-MP addresses. NOETHER's contribution is making construction algebra-induced and proving termination/decidability; the underlying goal is shared.

closest_prior_works.cite: Sun, Jin, Wu, Fu, Wang & Chan, Identifying metamorphic relations: a data mutation directed approach (muMT)
closest_prior_works.relation: State-of-the-art systematic MR-identification via data-mutation operators + template mapping rules. Direct competitor to NOETHER's identification goal. Differs in that muMT's operators are syntactic/data-mutation heuristics with no algebraic-closure or completeness theory; NOETHER claims structural derivation + provable well-formedness.

closest_prior_works.cite: Clark, Foster, Walkinshaw & Hierons, Metamorphic Testing with Causal Graphs
closest_prior_works.relation: Closest alternative principled MR-generator: uses causal DAGs (a different mathematical scaffold) to auto-generate MRs and reason about which faults are/aren't exposed. Parallels NOETHER's ambition (formal generator + reasoning about detection limits) via causal inference rather than operator algebra/group theory. Reviewers will expect NOETHER to contrast its operator-algebra scaffold against this causal-graph scaffold.

closest_prior_works.cite: Zhang, Chen, Hao, Xiong, Xie et al., Search-based inference of polynomial metamorphic relations
closest_prior_works.relation: Represents the MRs-as-inferable-invariants (polynomial relations) line; relevant because NOETHER's block invariants (additivity, monotonicity, linearity) overlap with the polynomial-invariant family inferred here. Differs: inference from execution data vs. derivation from a declared operator algebra.

closest_prior_works.cite: Ayerdi, Terragni, Jahangirova, Arrieta et al., GenMorph: Automatically Generating Metamorphic Relations via Genetic Programming
closest_prior_works.relation: Most recent automated MR-generation competitor; NOETHER explicitly relegates GenMorph/DeepCrime-style mutation results to secondary executability checks. Confirms NOETHER is aware of and positioning against the SBSE/mutation MR-generation line, the empirical (not theoretical) state of the art.

closest_prior_works.cite: Author self-sibling: Li, Yang, Liu & Yan, Minimum Complete MR Subsets under Semantic-Mutation Fault Models: A Support-Set Domination Boundary (arXiv 2606.08269); and the semantic-mutation-metric paper (arXiv 2605.17437)
closest_prior_works.relation: Companion P-series papers by the SAME authors sharing the fault-signature kernel / layer-relative completeness machinery. CRITICAL salami/self-overlap risk: NOETHER's Invariance-Blindness (detection kernel = commutant = structure-preserving faults) is adjacent to the sibling's minimum complete MR subset under a fault-signature kernel. NOETHER must cite these, draw a crisp boundary (generation/operator-algebra here vs. selection/minimal-subset there), and avoid re-deriving the sibling's completeness theory, or a reviewer will flag least-publishable-unit fragmentation.

closest_prior_works.cite: Zhu, Bayley, Liu & Zheng, Morphy: A Datamorphic Software Test Automation Tool (datamorphisms/metamorphisms as test morphisms)
closest_prior_works.relation: Only prior MT work framing test transformations in quasi-categorical morphism language (test entities + morphisms). Superficially adjacent to NOETHER's algebraic vocabulary, but an automation-architecture abstraction, NOT a group/operator-algebra theory, with no invariance/Noether/completeness content. Useful to cite to show NOETHER's algebra differs substantively from prior morphism terminology.

genuinely_novel: Importing Noether-style invariance and an explicit program-induced OPERATOR ALGEBRA A_P (named blocks: symmetry group G, monotone, linear, self-adjoint T*, time-reversal, limit, qualitative-dynamics, method-comparison, relational-equivalence) as the generator of MRs. No indexed SE paper builds MR identification on an operator algebra with this structure; prior symmetry framings stop at permutation/Lie symmetries (Gotlieb) or descriptive relation patterns (Segura).

The Invariance-Blindness Theorem (Thm 3): identifying an algebra-derived MR's detection kernel with the commutant C(T_s) = exactly the structure-preserving faults, within a linear fault class under a finite-test faithfulness condition, plus corollaries (single-block batteries incomplete; completeness needs oracle families with trivial joint kernel; cross-implementation differential oracle as the complementary common-mode oracle). A genuine negative/limiting result on what symmetry-derived oracles structurally CANNOT see; such impossibility theorems are essentially absent from the constructive/empirical MT literature.

Explicit FALSIFICATION of the absolute-completeness conjecture (Theorem 1') on a real safety algebra A_PWR via two concrete reactor-physics MRs (non-additivity of rod-bank reactivity worth; second-order mixed dependence of k_eff on moderator temperature and boron concentration), yielding five pairwise-independent structural obstructions in Translate's signature. Treating MR-framework completeness as a refutable formal claim and refuting it with domain-grounded counterexamples is methodologically distinctive.

Closure-under-Translate (Thm 1) + polynomial-time decidability of CONSTRUCT-MP (Thm 2) under a finite generating set, with a canonical-block total order assigning each algebra-induced MR to a unique MetaPattern. A by-construction well-formedness + complexity guarantee for MR generation is rare; prior constructive methods (Liu-Chen 2012, muMT 2023) give heuristics without termination/uniqueness theorems.

Deflationary use of the framework to DE-DUPLICATE / predict over-counted MRs (sorting library; re-decoding Murphy et al. 2008's six ML MR classes; the reactor catalogue itself). The over-counting-detection direction — showing an existing MR catalogue collapses under the algebra — is a novel diagnostic use of MR theory.
incremental_or_overlapping: The core intuition that MRs are symmetries/invariances of the program under input transformations is not new: explicit in Gotlieb's Symmetric Testing (2003/2006), in the Segura survey's relation patterns (2016), and the descriptive vocabulary of dozens of MT-for-ML papers (Spieker et al. 2024 trajectory-prediction symmetries; Naidu/Gudaparthi/Niu 2021 affine/noise MR classes; Hiremath et al. 2020 ocean-model symmetries). NOETHER's symmetry framing per se is incremental; only its formalization is new.

MRs-have-algebraic/composable-structure overlaps substantially with Qiu/Zheng/Chen TSE 2022 (MR composition theory) and Liu-Liu-Chen QSIC 2012 (constructing MRs by composition). NOETHER's closure-under-an-operator and canonical-ordering results extend, but do not orthogonally depart from, this program.

Systematic/structured MR identification overlaps with muMT (Sun et al. 2023), GenMorph (Ayerdi et al. 2024), polynomial-MR inference (Zhang et al. 2014), graph-kernel MR prediction, and the authors' own MR-recommendation work (Zhao et al. 2026). NOETHER differs by being theory-first rather than learning/search-first, but the problem and several relation families overlap.

The equivariance/group-symmetry instantiation on ML (C4) sits inside a large, mature equivariant-deep-learning literature (group-equivariant CNNs, E(3)/SO(3) networks, units-equivariance). Fresh as a testing contribution, but the symmetry objects themselves (Lie-group equivariance, permutation symmetry) are standard; the manuscript should avoid over-claiming novelty of the group concepts.

The fault-signature kernel / layer-relative completeness vocabulary overlaps with the authors' own sibling papers (arXiv 2606.08269, 2605.17437); risk of self-overlap rather than novelty unless the boundary is drawn sharply.

research.academic_level_verdict: TOSEM-worthy on this angle, CONDITIONALLY. The genuinely novel core — (a) deriving MRs from a program-induced operator algebra with closure + decidability theorems, (b) the Invariance-Blindness impossibility theorem characterizing the detection kernel as the commutant of structure-preserving faults, and (c) the formal falsification of an absolute-completeness conjecture via domain-grounded reactor-physics counterexamples — is a theory-first contribution of a kind the MT literature largely lacks (it is overwhelmingly constructive/empirical). This level of formal apparatus (impossibility result + by-construction guarantees) is appropriate for TOSEM. HOWEVER the contribution is theoretically deep but narrow on the angle: the symmetry/invariance reading of MRs is decades old (Gotlieb's Symmetric Testing; Segura's relation patterns), so the paper's value rests entirely on the formalization and the negative/limiting theory, NOT on the symmetry intuition. Three conditions gate acceptance: (1) it MUST cite and sharply differentiate from Symmetric Testing (Gotlieb 2003/2006; Patel-Hierons 2018) — currently the highest-risk omission; (2) it must draw a crisp boundary against the authors' own sibling minimum-complete-MR-subset / fault-kernel papers to dispel salami/self-overlap concerns; (3) the central theorems' applicability hinges on strong restrictions (linear operator-implementation fault class, faithfulness reachable by a finite test, finite generating set) — a TOSEM reviewer will scrutinize whether these leave the impossibility/completeness results meaningful for real programs beyond the reactor case study, and whether C4's structural transferability (explicitly not empirical superiority) is enough payoff for the formal machinery. If those are handled, the angle clears the TOSEM bar; if Symmetric Testing is ignored or the sibling boundary is fuzzy, it does not.

research.angle: MR-quality metrics (diversity / similarity / redundancy / fault-detection effectiveness), MR selection/prioritization/minimization (minimal MR subset), and any structural MR metric akin to SMS. Question: novelty of the paper's metrics/degeneration/minimization results vs existing MR-quality-metric and MR-minimization work.

closest_prior_works.cite: Nolasco, Molina, Degiovanni, Gorla, Garbervetsky, Papadakis, Uchitel, Aguirre, Frias — "Abstraction-Aware Inference of Metamorphic Relations" (MemoRIA)
closest_prior_works.relation: Closest prior work on the MR-MINIMIZATION axis. MemoRIA infers MRs from an object-protocol abstraction and then uses a SAT-based analysis to eliminate redundant relations, yielding a concise/minimal MR set with little impact on bug-finding ability — exactly the 'discard redundant MRs to get a minimal set' goal. NOETHER's 'deflationary over-counting' / de-duplication of MetaPatterns (m_adj, m_rev) and its subsumption-proportion evidence overlap conceptually, but NOETHER does minimization only descriptively (reports a subsumption proportion) and routes the actual minimization formalism to a sibling paper; MemoRIA already provides an executable, evaluated redundancy-elimination algorithm. Should be cited and contrasted.

closest_prior_works.cite: Li, Yang, Liu, Yan — "Minimum Complete MR Subsets under Semantic-Mutation Fault Models: A Support-Set Domination Boundary" (MINMR-COMPLETE)
closest_prior_works.relation: Same-author SIBLING paper that OWNS the minimization contribution: Min-MR-Complete formalized as Set-Cover-equivalent (NP-hard, log-approximation, greedy, exact ILP, plus an 'SMS-rank upper bound'). This is the salami boundary: NOETHER = MR generation/discovery from operator algebras (TOSEM); MINMR-COMPLETE = MR selection/minimization (TSE). Confirms that NOETHER itself makes essentially NO minimization claim. The two must cross-cite cleanly and NOETHER must not import this paper's hard theory, or it is double-counting a single contribution.

closest_prior_works.cite: Li, Yang, Liu, Yan — "A semantic mutation metric for metamorphic relation adequacy in scientific computing programs" (SMS)
closest_prior_works.relation: Same-author SIBLING paper that OWNS the structural-metric + DEGENERATION result the reviewer angle asks about: SMS is built on five domain-semantic mutation operators and is proved to 'degenerate almost everywhere to classical Mutation Score in a characterised limit' (backward compatibility). NOETHER references SMS-style evidence but the metric and its degeneration theorem live here, not in NOETHER. So NOETHER's own 'degeneration result' content is near-zero; the degeneration claim is this paper's, and TOSEM reviewers will need the boundary made explicit to avoid perceived self-overlap/salami.

closest_prior_works.cite: Xie, Li, Chen, Zhang, Wang et al. — "MUT Model: a metric for characterizing metamorphic relations diversity"
closest_prior_works.relation: Closest independent prior work on a STRUCTURAL MR-DIVERSITY METRIC (the 'SMS-like metric' axis). Explicitly defines a metric to characterize MR diversity and shows diversity-aware MR selection mitigates redundancy in fault detection. This is the direct competitor to any NOETHER/SMS structural metric claim and is currently a likely missing citation.

closest_prior_works.cite: Srinivasan & Kanewala — "Metamorphic relation prioritization for effective regression testing" (and the 2024 'data diversity-driven MR prioritization', Electronics)
closest_prior_works.venue_year: Softw. Testing Verif. Reliab. (STVR) 2021, DOI 10.1002/stvr.1807; Electronics 2024, DOI 10.3390/electronics13173380
closest_prior_works.relation: Defines fault-based and coverage/diversity-based MR prioritization, introduces five diversity metrics over source/follow-up cases, and explicitly removes redundant MRs. This is the mainstream MR-selection/prioritization-by-metric line that any MR-metric contribution must position against. NOETHER sidesteps it by demoting fault-detection to 'secondary executability checks', but the related-work positioning still needs it.

closest_prior_works.cite: Mayer & Guderlei — "An Empirical Study on the Selection of Good Metamorphic Relations"
closest_prior_works.relation: The seminal 'which MRs are good' selection study; foundational for any claim about MR quality/selection. Should be cited as the origin of MR-quality assessment that NOETHER's by-construction well-formedness reframes structurally rather than empirically.

closest_prior_works.cite: Asrafi, Liu & Kuo — "On Testing Effectiveness of Metamorphic Relations: A Case Study"
closest_prior_works.relation: Establishes the link between MR-induced execution-domain dissimilarity/coverage and fault-detection effectiveness — the conceptual root of MR diversity-as-quality. Relevant baseline for NOETHER's operator-block-coverage protocol and for any structural-coverage claim.

closest_prior_works.cite: Qiu, Zheng, Chen & Poon — "Theoretical and Empirical Analyses of the Effectiveness of Metamorphic Relation Composition"
closest_prior_works.relation: Closest THEORETICAL result on when combining MRs preserves vs degrades fault-detection capability (a 'closure-under-composition'-flavored theorem). NOETHER's Theorem 1 (no-drop closure under Translate) is a different operator (Translate, not composition) and a weaker by-construction well-formedness claim, but reviewers will compare the two; must be cited and the distinction (closure of the MR space under a generation operator vs fault-detection preservation under composition) stated precisely.

closest_prior_works.cite: Shi, Chen, Fang, Feng & Xu — "Measuring the Diversity of a Test Set With Distance Entropy"
closest_prior_works.relation: Canonical structural diversity metric (distance entropy) validated against fault detection via mutation analysis. Methodological precedent for any entropy/diversity structural metric; relevant to the SMS/MUT lineage and to NOETHER's subsumption/coverage evidence.

closest_prior_works.cite: Zhang, Chen, Hao, Xiong, Xie, Zhang, Mei — "Search-based inference of polynomial metamorphic relations"
closest_prior_works.relation: Foundational systematic/automatic MR-generation baseline (search-based, polynomial MRs). NOETHER's CONSTRUCT-MP is a constructive algebraic alternative; the manuscript's 'search-vs-NOETHER origin/boundary comparison' (C5) implicitly competes with this line, so it is a required baseline citation for the generation side that frames the metric/coverage protocol.

closest_prior_works.cite: Segura, Fraser, Sanchez & Ruiz-Cortes — "A Survey on Metamorphic Testing"
closest_prior_works.relation: Explicitly names 'techniques to remove redundant metamorphic relations' and MR subsumption relationships as OPEN PROBLEMS. Directly frames the novelty space for both the redundancy/minimization angle and the MR-pattern catalogue angle; canonical citation and a natural foil for positioning NOETHER's de-duplication.

genuinely_novel: The de-duplication / 'deflationary over-counting' direction is framed via a generative mechanism (an operator algebra whose canonical-block ordering forces every MR into a UNIQUE MetaPattern — Theorem 1), rather than post-hoc redundancy elimination (MemoRIA's SAT pruning) or distance-based diversity scoring (MUT, Srinivasan-Kanewala). Predicting that two inductively-catalogued MetaPatterns collapse to one (m_adj, m_rev) FROM algebraic structure, and demonstrating over-counting on three independent catalogues (sorting library; Murphy et al. 2008's six ML MR classes; the reactor catalogue), is a structural-uniqueness argument not present in the metric/minimization literature.

An evidence protocol that deliberately treats MR-identification quality as operator-BLOCK COVERAGE (binary expert-vs-NOETHER) and origin/boundary, and explicitly DEMOTES mutation/GenMorph/DeepCrime fault-detection numbers to 'secondary executability checks rather than evidence of average fault-detection superiority' — i.e. it refuses the standard fault-detection-effectiveness metric as the headline. This honest reframing (well-formedness/coverage, not effectiveness) is a defensible and unusual stance versus the diversity/prioritization line that all anchors on fault-detection effectiveness.

The Invariance-Blindness Theorem (Theorem 3): an algebra-derived MR's detection kernel equals exactly the structure-preserving (commutant) faults within a linear fault class — a kernel-exactness LIMITING result with corollaries (single-block batteries incomplete; completeness needs trivial joint kernel; differential oracle is the complementary blind spot). This is a fault-CLASS characterization tied to operator structure, qualitatively different from empirical MR-quality metrics and from Set-Cover minimization; no direct prior analogue framed as an exact detection-kernel = commutant equality was found.
incremental_or_overlapping: The actual MR-MINIMIZATION contribution is NOT in this manuscript — it is in the same authors' sibling MINMR-COMPLETE (arXiv:2606.08269), which formalizes Min-MR-Complete as Set-Cover-equivalent (NP-hard, greedy/ILP, SMS-rank bound). Within NOETHER, minimization appears only as a reported subsumption proportion (94.4%, Wilson CI). So on the minimization angle NOETHER's standalone novelty is thin/descriptive; the risk is salami-perception unless the boundary is crisply cited.

The structural-METRIC and DEGENERATION content (SMS degenerating to classical Mutation Score in a limit) lives in the sibling SMS paper (arXiv:2605.17437), not in NOETHER. The reviewer's 'degeneration result' is therefore largely outside this manuscript; what remains inside is the qualitative de-duplication, which overlaps in spirit with MemoRIA's redundancy elimination and MUT's diversity metric.

Reproducing three prior MetaPatterns and refining two (C3) is, on the metric axis, a re-classification of an existing inductive catalogue rather than a new quantitative MR-quality metric; the diversity/coverage notions used (subsumption proportion, block coverage) are operationalized with established constructs (subsumption — Segura survey; coverage/diversity — Asrafi-Liu-Kuo, Shi distance entropy).

Theorem 1's 'no-drop closure under Translate' is a by-construction well-formedness guarantee explicitly disclaimed as NOT fault-detection superiority; as such it does not advance the fault-detection-effectiveness metric literature and partially overlaps in motivation (closure/preservation flavor) with Qiu-Zheng-Chen-Poon's composition-preservation theorem, against which it must be distinguished.

research.academic_level_verdict: On THIS reviewer's specific angle (MR-quality metrics / diversity / redundancy / minimization / SMS-like structural metric), NOETHER's standalone contribution is NOT the strong part of the paper and is, by design, mostly hosted in two sibling papers (SMS metric+degeneration in arXiv:2605.17437; minimum-complete MR subset in arXiv:2606.08269). Inside NOETHER itself the metric/minimization content reduces to (a) a qualitative 'deflationary over-counting' de-duplication argument and (b) a descriptive subsumption proportion — both of which overlap conceptually with MemoRIA (SAT redundancy elimination, FSE 2024) and MUT (MR-diversity metric, 2024), neither currently cited. That overlap, plus the salami risk across the three same-author preprints, is a real but FIXABLE concern: it requires explicit cross-citation and a sharp boundary statement, not new science. Crucially, NOETHER's genuine TOSEM-level contribution is on a DIFFERENT axis than this reviewer's: constructive MR/MetaPattern DISCOVERY from a program-induced operator algebra, with a positive closure theorem (Thm 1), a decidability result (Thm 2), a negative completeness refutation on a real safety-critical algebra (Thm 1' false on A_PWR), and the exact-detection-kernel Invariance-Blindness Theorem (Thm 3). Those are theory-grade and plausibly TOSEM-worthy. So: the metrics/degeneration/minimization angle alone is NOT independently TOSEM-worthy (it is incremental and partly off-loaded to siblings), but it is not the paper's load-bearing claim; the paper should down-scope its metric/minimization language, cite MemoRIA/MUT/Srinivasan-Kanewala, and lean on the constructive-discovery + negative-completeness + invariance-blindness theory, which is where TOSEM-level novelty actually resides.

research.angle: Equivariance/invariance testing of ML and equivariant-ML theory; the manuscript's "Invariance-Blindness Theorem" (Thm 3) and the equivariant-ML instantiation (algebra A_equi exercising the Lie-group / symmetry-G and self-adjoint-T* blocks). The question is whether, relative to the equivariant-ML and DL-metamorphic-testing literatures, (a) the equivariance instantiation and (b) the blindness/degeneration theorem are novel.

closest_prior_works.cite: Gruver, Finzi, Goldblum, Wilson — The Lie Derivative for Measuring Learned Equivariance
closest_prior_works.relation: CLOSEST equivariant-ML measurement work. Introduces the Lie derivative as a principled, low-hyperparameter way to MEASURE how much a trained model's prediction violates a continuous symmetry (translation/rotation), and traces violations to aliasing in pointwise nonlinearities. Overlaps the manuscript's quantitative side (equivariance-violation as a signal) and its claim that the symmetry/G-block is the natural locus for ML. BUT it measures the degree of equivariance of a model; it does not frame symmetry as a test ORACLE, does not define a detection kernel, and proves no completeness/blind-spot result. The manuscript's IBT (detection kernel = commutant C(T_s) = structure-preserving faults) is a fault-detection-completeness statement Gruver et al. never make. Almost certainly a MISSING citation.

closest_prior_works.cite: Kaba & Ravanbakhsh — Symmetry Breaking and Equivariant Neural Networks
closest_prior_works.relation: CLOSEST equivariant-ML LIMITATION theorem. Proves equivariant functions cannot break symmetry at the level of individual samples (a representational/expressivity limitation of equivariant maps). Conceptually adjacent to the IBT's message that symmetry constrains what is visible, but the object is different: their limitation is about what an equivariant MODEL can output; the IBT is about what an equivariant-derived TEST can detect (which faults lie in the oracle's kernel). Distinct claim; strong candidate to cite as related limitation theory.

closest_prior_works.cite: Balachandar, Poulenard, Deng, Guibas — Breaking the Symmetry: Resolving Symmetry Ambiguities in Equivariant Neural Networks (OAVNN)
closest_prior_works.relation: Identifies a 'fundamental limitation' of equivariant networks: ambiguity to symmetric inputs (cannot segment a left-right symmetric object). Same genre as the IBT (symmetry induces a blind/ambiguous subspace) but again about model capability, not test detection power. Useful as a second instance of 'symmetry → structural blind spot' to position the IBT against.

closest_prior_works.cite: Saha & Kanewala — Fault Detection Effectiveness of Metamorphic Relations Developed for Testing Supervised Classifiers
closest_prior_works.relation: EMPIRICAL analogue of the IBT for ML. Shows MRs for supervised classifiers detect only ~14.8% of reachable mutants, i.e. most faults are invisible to the MRs. This is exactly the phenomenon the IBT explains structurally (the detection kernel excludes a large fault subspace), but Saha & Kanewala give no formal characterization of WHICH faults are missed. The manuscript should cite this as the empirical precedent that its theorem rationalizes.

closest_prior_works.cite: Murphy, Kaiser, Hu, Wu — Properties of Machine Learning Applications for Use in Metamorphic Testing
closest_prior_works.relation: Explicitly RE-DECODED by the manuscript (C3 'six ML MR classes re-decoded'). The canonical inductive catalogue of ML MR classes (additive, multiplicative, permutative, invertive, inclusive, exclusive). The manuscript's deflationary claim is that these reduce to fewer operator-algebra blocks. Must be cited (and apparently is). The novelty rests on the constructive/algebraic re-derivation, not on the MR classes themselves.

closest_prior_works.cite: Tian, Pei, Jana, Ray — DeepTest; Deng et al. — RMT: A Declarative Rule-based Metamorphic Testing Framework for Autonomous Driving
closest_prior_works.relation: Representative DL-metamorphic-testing instantiations using invariance/transformation MRs (image transforms, traffic-rule MRs). Establish that 'apply symmetry/invariance MRs to a DL system' is well-trodden. They make the equivariance INSTANTIATION (manuscript C4 on A_equi) incremental: deriving translation/rotation/scale invariance MRs for an equivariant-ML algebra is not itself new; only the algebra-skeleton derivation framing is.

closest_prior_works.cite: Li, Liu, Poon, Towey, Sun, Zheng, Zhou, Chen — Metamorphic Relation Generation: State of the Art and Visions for Future Research
closest_prior_works.relation: Authoritative survey of MR generation. Frames the manuscript's CONSTRUCT-MP (constructive MR derivation from an operator algebra) against the field's mostly-search/ML/template-based generators. Needed to substantiate the claim that constructive, theory-driven MR derivation with closure/decidability guarantees is under-explored. Likely a missing positioning citation.

closest_prior_works.cite: Ayerdi, Terragni, Jahangirova, Arrieta, Tonella — GenMorph: Automatically Generating Metamorphic Relations via Genetic Programming
closest_prior_works.relation: State-of-the-art automatic MR generator; the manuscript treats GenMorph-style results as secondary executability checks (C5). Defines the search-based baseline the manuscript contrasts its constructive approach against. Appropriate to cite; not a novelty threat to the theorem.

genuinely_novel: The Invariance-Blindness Theorem (Thm 3): a FORMAL identification, for the symmetry-G and self-adjoint-T* blocks, that an algebra-derived MR's detection kernel equals exactly the commutant C(T_s) = the structure-preserving faults (within a linear-implementation fault class, under a finite-test faithfulness condition). No work in the equivariant-ML or DL-MT literature proves a fault-detection-completeness/blind-spot theorem of this form. Equivariant-ML limitation theorems (Kaba-Ravanbakhsh, Balachandar) constrain model expressivity, not test detection power; Saha-Kanewala observe low MR fault-detection empirically but give no kernel characterization; Gruver et al. measure equivariance but make no oracle-completeness claim.

The three corollaries operationalizing the IBT: (i) single-block batteries are incomplete; (ii) completeness requires oracle families with trivial joint kernel; (iii) a cross-implementation differential oracle is the complementary (common-mode) blind spot. Casting differential testing as the structurally-determined complement of an invariance oracle is a non-obvious, theory-grounded contribution not present in the DL-MT differential/metamorphic-testing comparisons (e.g., Ahuja-Gotlieb-Spieker).

Treating equivariance/invariance MRs as the Translate-image of a program-induced operator algebra (the G and T* blocks of A_equi), giving closure (Thm 1) and polynomial-time decidability (Thm 2) for the MR-construction itself. The constructive, guaranteed-well-formedness derivation of invariance MRs is a different epistemic object than the inductive/search-based MR catalogues that dominate DL-MT.

The deflationary (over-counting) demonstration applied to Murphy et al. 2008's six ML MR classes — re-decoding an established ML-MT catalogue as a smaller set of algebra blocks — is a novel analytic use of the framework on the ML side, beyond merely adding new MRs.
incremental_or_overlapping: The equivariant-ML INSTANTIATION as an empirical/testing artifact (deriving translation/rotation/scale/permutation invariance MRs for an equivariant-ML algebra) is incremental: applying symmetry/invariance MRs to DL systems is extensively done (DeepTest, RMT, Spieker et al. trajectory MT, METAL for LLMs, GAN/deepfake-fairness MT). Per the manuscript's own framing (C4 = 'structural transferability at the algebra-skeleton level, not cross-domain empirical superiority'), the instantiation is a feasibility demonstration, not a new testing capability — and at 'differentiated depth' the A_equi treatment appears shallower than the reactor-physics core, so it carries little independent novelty weight.

The idea that symmetry/equivariance induces a structural blind spot overlaps thematically with the equivariant-ML limitation theorems (Kaba-Ravanbakhsh symmetry-breaking impossibility; Balachandar symmetry ambiguity). The manuscript's contribution is the precise testing-theoretic restatement (kernel = commutant), but reviewers from the equivariant-ML community will see the 'symmetry constrains what is detectable' intuition as familiar; novelty must be defended as the exact-kernel/oracle-completeness result, not the intuition.

Quantifying equivariance violation as a detection signal overlaps with Gruver et al.'s Lie derivative and Myburgh et al.'s translation-sensitivity maps. If the manuscript uses any continuous-symmetry violation magnitude on A_equi without citing these, it overlaps prior measurement methodology.

Using mutation/GenMorph/DeepCrime-style results as executability checks is standard practice (DeepMutation, GenMorph); no novelty there, and the manuscript correctly demotes them to secondary evidence.
