Kaba & Ravanbakhsh, 'Symmetry Breaking and Equivariant Neural Networks', NeurIPS 2023 (arXiv:2312.09016) — closest equivariant-ML limitation theorem; needed to distinguish model-expressivity limits from the IBT's test-detection limit.
Balachandar et al., 'Breaking the Symmetry: Resolving Symmetry Ambiguities in Equivariant Neural Networks', 2022 (arXiv:2210.16646) — second symmetry-induced-blind-spot limitation in equivariant ML.

Saha & Kanewala, 'Fault Detection Effectiveness of Metamorphic Relations Developed for Testing Supervised Classifiers', 2019 (arXiv:1904.07348) — empirical precedent for low MR fault-detection that the IBT explains structurally; strongest missing empirical anchor on the ML side.

Li, Liu, Poon, Towey, Sun, Zheng, Zhou, Chen, 'Metamorphic Relation Generation: State of the Art and Visions', 2024 (arXiv:2406.05397) — needed to substantiate the under-explored-ness of constructive MR derivation.

Tian, Pei, Jana, Ray, 'DeepTest', ICSE 2018 and/or Deng et al. 'RMT' (arXiv:2012.10672) — to acknowledge that invariance-MR-based DL testing is established, so the equivariance instantiation is positioned honestly as incremental.

(Recommended) Myburgh, Mouton, Davel, 'Tracking translation invariance in CNNs', 2021 (arXiv:2104.05997) — alternative equivariance/invariance measurement, if the manuscript reports any invariance-sensitivity metric on A_equi.
research.academic_level_verdict: On this angle the contribution is TOSEM-worthy, but the worth is carried almost entirely by the THEORY (Theorem 3 / IBT and its corollaries), not by the equivariant-ML instantiation. The IBT — characterizing an invariance-based MR oracle's detection kernel as exactly the commutant/structure-preserving fault subspace, and deriving from it that single-block batteries are incomplete and that a differential oracle is the structurally complementary blind spot — is, to the best of the searched literature, a genuinely new result. Equivariant-ML limitation theorems (Kaba-Ravanbakhsh, Balachandar) constrain model expressivity; equivariance-measurement tools (Gruver et al., Myburgh et al.) quantify violation; MR fault-detection studies (Saha-Kanewala) observe low detection empirically — but none formally identifies which fault subspace is invisible to a symmetry/self-adjoint oracle. That gap is real and the manuscript fills it with a clean operator-algebraic statement, which is the kind of conceptual/formal contribution TOSEM values. CAVEATS that gate acceptance: (1) the equivariant-ML instantiation per se is incremental and must be presented (as the authors largely do) as feasibility/transferability, not as new testing power, or a strong equivariant-ML reviewer will discount it; (2) the IBT's scope conditions (linear operator-implementation fault class, finite-test faithfulness) are restrictive — generalization beyond linear faults is unproven, and reviewers will press on how much of real ML fault space this covers; (3) the missing equivariant-ML citations above are currently a defensibility risk — without Gruver et al. and Kaba-Ravanbakhsh the related-work will read as unaware of the equivariant-ML community, which for a TOSEM cross-domain claim is a credibility problem. Conditional on tightening the theorem's stated scope and adding the missing citations, the angle clears the TOSEM novelty bar.

reviews.summary: The manuscript is a theory-forward MR-identification framework (operator-algebra → MetaPattern derivation) with three headline theorems and a multi-pronged empirical layer. Its single greatest soundness strength is unusual honesty: nearly every weakness a critical referee would raise is self-disclosed, scoped, and demoted in advance (Theorem 1 admitted "by-construction," pilots labeled underpowered with Wilson CIs and McNemar/Fisher p-values, the head-to-head loss to GenMorph reported plainly, self-implementation/LLM-rater confounds stated in Threats). This is what keeps it at a borderline-3 rather than below. However, three soundness problems remain that are not fully neutralized by disclosure. (1) The flagship "non-tautological" result, the Invariance-Blindness Theorem, is near-circular as stated: "faithfulness" is *defined* as ker(ρ)=C(T_s) and the theorem then concludes ker(ρ)=C(T_s) under faithfulness; the genuine content lives entirely in the Reachability Lemma, which the theorem statement should absorb. (2) "Polynomial-time decidability" (Theorem 2) is stated as a headline contribution but the per-generator cost is O(|G|^2) for finite groups, and |G| is exponential in the number of generators, so the bound is polynomial in output/group size, not input size; the Lie/truncation prose scopes this but the headline term recurs unqualified in the abstract, intro, and conclusion. (3) The "central" empirical L*-blindness result is a confirmation of an a-priori mathematical theorem (kill rate ≈ 0 by construction), so its empirical "5/6 SUTs confirmed" carries little independent evidential weight, and the one outlier (hypotSig 2/4) is rescued by a homogeneity-breaking reclassification rule codified after the analysis it retroactively justifies — a mild selection-on-the-response pattern. The theory↔experiment coupling is loose throughout (grand operator-algebra theory vs. PIT mutants on toy Java/EGNN subjects), but this is honestly framed as "secondary executability." Net: methodologically careful and transparent, but the two strongest theorems are weaker than their headline phrasing implies, which a strict TOSEM referee must require fixed before acceptance.

findings.issue: The Invariance-Blindness Theorem is the paper's designated non-tautological theoretical contribution (C2c), but as stated it is near-circular. Definition (Faithfulness) reads: a finite witness set is faithful iff ker(ρ_{ι,s})=C(T_s). Theorem IBT then concludes ker(ρ_{ι,s})=C(T_s)=C(T_s) 'given faithful witnesses.' The conclusion is literally the assumption. The proof's ⊆ direction is one line that simply invokes the faithfulness definition. All genuine mathematical content is in Lemma (Reachability of faithfulness) — that a finite faithful witness set EXISTS — which the paper itself flags ('Lemma is the crux: tightness is not tautological but follows from finite fault-dimensionality').
findings.evidence: Def: 'A finite witness set W^test_s is faithful iff ker(ρ_{ι,s})=C(T_s)'. Theorem: '...let the test witnesses be faithful (Definition...). Then ker(ρ_{ι,s})=C(T_s)=...'. Proof ⊆: 'If L∈ker then E_s(L;w)=0 on W^test_s; by faithfulness ... ker(ρ_{ι,s})=C(T_s), so L∈C(T_s).'
findings.suggested_fix: Restate the theorem so the load-bearing claim is the Reachability Lemma's conclusion (a finite executable witness set attains the exact blind set C(T_s)), making faithfulness a proven property rather than a hypothesis whose statement coincides with the conclusion. Either fold the lemma into the theorem as its main clause, or drop 'faithful' as a hypothesis and conclude existence of a finite W^test with ker=C(T_s). As written, the theorem cannot be cited as 'falsifiable, non-tautological' (its abstract/intro framing) without this restructuring.

findings.section: §3.3.3 Theorem 2 (Decidability) + Table (Per-block invariant-extraction cost); also Abstract/Intro/Conclusion 'polynomial-time'
findings.issue: The contribution is repeatedly headlined as 'polynomial-time decidability of CONSTRUCT-MP.' The proven bound is O(n·max_i t_i·log n) where n = number of GENERATORS, but the per-generator cost for the symmetry block is t_i=O(|G|^2) for finite groups. |G| is exponential in n for many finitely generated groups (e.g. (Z_2)^k has |G|=2^k from k generators). So the bound is polynomial in (n, |G|, d, K), i.e. in output/group size, not in input size — the standard meaning of 'polynomial-time' for a decidability claim. The Lie-group O(d_G^2) and infinite-discrete truncation O(K^2) prose correctly scopes this, but the unqualified term propagates to the abstract, the five-contribution list, the boundary boxes, and the conclusion.
findings.evidence: Theorem 2: 'O(n·max_i t_i·log n)'. Cost table first row: 'finite group | O(|G|^2) (group-orbit fixed-point)'. Prose: 'The asymptotic bound is therefore not the binding constraint in either instantiation' (i.e. finite small |G| in the instances), but Conclusion box still asserts '(ii) polynomial-time decidability under finite generating-set assumption.'
findings.suggested_fix: Qualify every headline occurrence to 'polynomial in the generating-set and group/output size' or 'fixed-parameter / output-polynomial,' and state explicitly in Theorem 2 that t_i may be exponential in n for finite groups whose order is exponential in their generator count. Without this, a referee will read 'polynomial-time' as input-polynomial, which is not what is proved.

findings.issue: The 'central' falsifiable empirical claim (L*-block blindness) is rescued on its single failing SUT by a reclassification rule that was codified after the analysis it retroactively legitimizes — a selection-on-the-response / HARKing-adjacent pattern. hypotSig kills 2/4, above the pre-registered 1/3 per-SUT falsification threshold; it is salvaged by declaring both killed mutants 'homogeneity-breaking,' under an 'outlier-handling rule' the paper admits was written down only on 2026-05-15 to make explicit a rule 'on which the hypotSig analysis had relied in implicit rather than written form.'
findings.evidence: 'The rule was codified in the pre-registration config on 2026-05-15 to make explicit a rule on which the §...hypotSig analysis had relied in implicit rather than written form. Under the codified rule, hypotSig's two killed mutants ... both classify as homogeneity-breaking, so the original 5/6 verdict stands.'
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) report the verdict both with and without the outlier-rescue rule and let the unrescued count stand as the primary (5/6 with one genuine over-threshold SUT), or (b) re-run on a fresh, never-inspected SUT substrate where the homogeneity-breaking classification is applied strictly ex-ante. Also note that since the L*-blindness 'prediction' is itself a derived mathematical consequence (kill rate identically 0 by construction), the empirical test is closer to a sanity check of the implementation than a falsification opportunity for the theory; frame it as such rather than as 'a quantitative consequence ... empirically operative as a mechanism.'

findings.section: §3.3 Theorem 1 (Algebraic Closure) framing across Abstract/Intro/Boundary boxes
findings.issue: Theorem 1 is logically a near-tautology: MR(A_P) is DEFINED as the Translate-image of block invariants (Def. alg-induced), so 'every ρ∈MR(A_P) is assigned to some m∈M(A_P)' restates the construction. This is appropriately and repeatedly self-disclosed, so it is not a blocker, but the abstract and the C2a contribution still present it with theorem-grade prominence ('Theorem 1 proves a no-drop closure invariant') that a reader may over-weight before reaching the L599 acknowledgement.
findings.evidence: L599: 'A sceptical reading might object that the by-construction status of Theorem 1 makes it near-tautological. We acknowledge that the closure result is by-construction within the explicit scope of Definition...'. Uniqueness proof reduces to 'strict total order on a finite set by inspection.'
findings.suggested_fix: In the abstract and contribution list, label Theorem 1 explicitly as a well-formedness/closure-by-construction guarantee (as the body already does), so the theorem-grade prominence matches its admitted modesty. The honest disclosure already exists; just propagate it to the headline statements.

findings.section: §4.4.x five pairwise-independent obstructions (Table obstruction set) + §3.5 third-domain ten dimensions
findings.issue: The 'five pairwise-independent structural obstructions' are established by per-block exhaustion only for the two A_PWR counterexamples; the additional 'five candidate dimensions' on A_equi and A_rel have pairwise-independence 'asserted by inspection rather than by formal exhaustion proof.' The aggregate framing ('ten Translate-extension dimensions') risks over-counting independence the proofs do not establish. Independence of the PWR five is also partly definitional: three of them (operator-spectrum output, homomorphism-failure π-template, configuration-indexed adjoint) all derive from the single fact that k_eff is a spectral quantity of a configuration-indexed operator family, so 'pairwise independent' deserves a sharper criterion than 'no single Translate extension covers two rows.'
findings.evidence: 'five Translate-extension dimensions proved pairwise-independent on A_PWR plus five candidate dimensions ... whose pairwise independence is asserted by inspection; formal per-dimension exhaustion on those algebras is committed as follow-up.' Obstruction table rows O1/O2/O3 all trace to the k_eff-as-eigenvalue / configuration-indexed-operator root cause described in the §6.1 perturbation reading.
findings.suggested_fix: State the independence criterion precisely (e.g. 'no extension repairing obstruction i validates ρ for any instance blocked solely by obstruction j') and verify it for at least one pair among O1/O2/O3, since they share the spectral-quantity origin. Downgrade the cross-algebra 'ten dimensions' language to 'five proven + five conjectured' wherever it appears in headline form (abstract/intro/conclusion), matching the body's honest qualification.

findings.section: §4.3 case study + §4.3.1 DeepCrime pilot + §5 external validity (commons-math)
findings.issue: Several empirical arms are underpowered and/or construct-validity-controlled, and the inferential statistics correctly show non-significance; these are honestly reported, so the issue is residual rather than disqualifying. The risk is that a hurried reader takes the case-study 7/20-vs-0/20 (Set N vs Set B, Fisher p=0.008) or the 2/5 pilot as effectiveness evidence despite the construct-validity caveat that the mutation set was built one-category-per-block with cat-(iv) chosen because ρ_train-rev alone covers it.
findings.evidence: Pilot: 'two-sided exact p=0.500 ... underpowered for an inferential conclusion at α=0.05 ... reported as descriptive evidence.' Case study: 'the mutation set was constructed to cover one defect category per non-empty block ... so cat-(iv)'s category was selected because ρ_train-rev alone covers it.' commons-math: 'n is underpowered for α=0.05 hypothesis testing.'
findings.suggested_fix: No new analysis required; ensure the abstract/intro never cite the case-study or pilot detection numbers as evidence for identification superiority (they currently do not, which is correct). Consider consolidating the construct-validity caveat into a single sentence at first mention to prevent partial quotation of the favorable cell. Compliant with the project's own C6 underpowered-pilot rule.

findings.section: Related Work 2.4 (MetaPattern catalogues) and Intro novelty framing
findings.issue: A directly competing MR-derivation taxonomy is uncited: Khritankov and Iakusheva, A systematic review of methods for deriving metamorphic relations (Program Systems: Theory and Applications, 2024, DOI 10.25209/2079-3316-2024-15-2-37-86), surveys methods for deriving MRs and proposes a classification of MRs into six basic types plus typical input transformations. This is the same conceptual target (where MRs come from) and the same finite-type-list move as NOETHER's block taxonomy; its omission overstates the novelty delta and leaves the closest published cousin to the block-taxonomy idea unaddressed.
findings.evidence: Intro asserts None of the existing MP proposals answers the three questions (origin/closure/transferability); 2.4 enumerates only Zhou2020, Lin2018, Ying2025 as closest cousins and even concedes three other candidates could not be located through the standard fallback chain, signaling the related-work net was not exhaustive on derivation taxonomies.
findings.suggested_fix: Add and engage Khritankov & Iakusheva (2024): state how NOETHER's eight algebra-derived blocks differ from their six inductively-surveyed MR types (the delta being the operator-algebra source + Translate closure + IBT, not the existence of a finite type list), and re-run a derivation-taxonomy-focused related-work search to confirm no other competing classification is missed.

findings.section: 3.3.3 Remark Scope of Theorem 1 and the sceptical-reading paragraph (L596-601)
findings.issue: The headline positive theorem (Thm 1, Algebraic Closure under Translate) is, by the authors own admission, near-tautological because MR(A_P) is defined as the Translate-image of block invariants; closure of CONSTRUCT-MP over its own image carries little novel content. As the load-bearing theory contribution it adds limited genuine novelty, while the substantive novelty (IBT and the negative PWR falsification) is under-weighted in the contribution ordering (C2a listed first/primary).
findings.evidence: Author text: A sceptical reading might object that the by-construction status of Theorem 1 makes it near-tautological. We acknowledge that the closure result is by-construction within the explicit scope of Definition 7 (which fixes MR(A_P) as the Translate-image of A_P). C2a is itself labeled intentionally modest ... a well-formedness guarantee.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-rank contributions so the IBT (Thm 3) and the falsified absolute-completeness Thm 1-prime (five pairwise-independent obstructions proved by per-block exhaustion) are framed as the primary theoretical novelty, and demote Thm 1 to a well-formedness lemma, so reviewers do not read the flagship theorem as definitional.

findings.section: 3.5-3.7 three domain instantiations and 3.4.3 note on prediction (interpretive caveat)
findings.issue: The cross-domain breadth (claimed novelty C4) is largely repackaging of known invariants. The paper concedes the Boltzmann m_adj/m_rev predictions are circular (the self-adjoint and time-reversal blocks were curated from reactor physics), the equivariant-ML MetaPatterns correspond to invariants independently validated in the equivariant-ML literature (G-CNN/EGNN/SE(3)-Transformer/reversible nets), and the relational MRs are already in the published optimiser-equivalence literature (SPES/QED/Calcite). The novel element reduces to a uniform algebraic warrant, a thinner delta than three structurally distinct instantiations implies.
findings.evidence: L716: There is therefore a circularity in the strong reading of prediction ... The framework does not discover these MetaPatterns de novo. L784/L896 explicitly describe equivariant and relational MRs as not de-novo MR discovery but the uniform algebraic warrant. Prior-art check confirms rotation-invariance/equivariance MT for DNNs is well-established (statistical-MT CNN work; 3D rotation invariance/equivariance surveys).
findings.suggested_fix: Reframe C4 as uniform re-derivation across three algebraic skeletons rather than transferability evidence carrying novelty weight, and foreground the genuinely novel items (rho_adj adjoint-attention duality and rho_train-rev training-reversal, claimed uncatalogued) as the only domain contributions with real novelty, with an explicit literature check substantiating their absence.

findings.issue: The Noether-style derivation framing (conserved-current-as-MR; symmetry implies invariant MR) is presented as distinctive, but symmetry-group-derived MRs are prior art (Zhou et al. 2020 symmetry metamorphic relation pattern; the equivariant-ML invariance literature). The delta over Zhou 2020 is asserted but not directly contrasted in the symmetry-derivation subsections, so the framing reads as more novel than it is.
findings.evidence: L745: instead of cataloguing observed invariants, derive them from a structural source. Zhou2020SymmetryMRP is cited only in 2.4 as introducing an explicit symmetry metamorphic relation pattern as a reusable abstraction for deriving concrete MRs across applications, the same derive-from-symmetry idea, but is not engaged at 3.4.1 / 3.5 Step 5b where NOETHER makes its own symmetry-derivation claim.
findings.suggested_fix: In 3.4.1 / 3.4.4 add one sentence contrasting NOETHER's G-block derivation with Zhou 2020's symmetry MR pattern, making the delta concrete (closed Translate operator + IBT kernel characterization vs a named reusable pattern) so the symmetry-framing novelty is anchored.

findings.section: 2.5 Relation to a separate line of work on minimum complete MR subsets (salami boundary)
findings.issue: Salami-slicing risk against the sibling P-series minimum complete MR subset paper is present (overlapping authors, shared MR/MT infrastructure) but handled well: the boundary is explicit (generation/derivation vs selection/minimization) and the paper states no theorem or empirical claim is shared. Per instruction this self-disclosed, bounded concern is down-graded; it is not a novelty blocker as written, provided the sibling paper is cited once public.
findings.evidence: L328-342: A separate line of work by some of the present authors addresses the orthogonal problem of selecting a minimum complete subset ... The two are complementary: NOETHER generates the algebra-induced MR space that a subset-selection procedure would then minimise. No theorem or empirical claim is shared.
findings.suggested_fix: At submission, cite the sibling subset-selection paper with a stable identifier (or as under review, anonymised) so reviewers can verify the non-overlap claim rather than take it on assertion; keep the explicit no-shared-claim sentence.

reviews.summary: The central novel idea is genuine: a constructive framework (CONSTRUCT-MP plus a defined Translate operator) deriving MetaPatterns / MR classes from a program-induced operator algebra, with three theorems: a no-drop closure invariant (Thm 1), poly-time decidability (Thm 2), and the Invariance-Blindness Theorem (IBT, Thm 3). The IBT is the strongest and least-anticipated contribution: it characterizes the detection kernel of an algebra-induced symmetry/self-adjoint MR as exactly the structure-preserving fault set, with a faithfulness lemma showing a finite test attains tightness. To my knowledge this analytical characterization of what an invariance-MR is blind to is not present in the MR-pattern literature and is a real delta over prior taxonomies (METRIC/METRIC+, Zhou 2020 symmetry MR pattern, Ying 2025 family trees, Segura 2019 query-MR patterns). However, the novelty is materially diluted by three things the paper itself concedes: (i) the eight operator blocks are an admitted empirical curation (Hypothesis 1), not derived, so the derivation sits downstream of a still-inductive taxonomy; (ii) all three domain instantiations are explicitly not de novo discoveries but re-labeling of textbook-canonical invariants under an algebraic vocabulary, and the flagship closure theorem is self-described as by-construction / near-tautological; (iii) the equivariant-ML and relational instantiations re-derive invariances already standard in those fields. A directly competing MR-derivation taxonomy (Khritankov and Iakusheva 2024, classifying MRs into six basic types) is not cited. Net: a borderline-but-defensible TOSEM novelty contribution carried almost entirely by the IBT and the constructive/closure framing; the breadth claims are largely repackaging. Salami-slicing against the sibling minimum complete MR subset line is cleanly disclosed and bounded (generation vs selection) and is not a blocker.

NOETHER reframes MR identification as a deductive derivation from a program-family operator algebra, with a closure theorem, a polynomial-time decidability result, and a falsified absolute-completeness conjecture. The conceptual move (lifting induction from MR-instance to algebra-block level) is genuinely interesting and the scope discipline is unusually honest: the paper repeatedly and correctly disclaims fault-detection superiority and frames its claim as MR-identification design-space coverage plus origin/boundary auditability. The problem for SIGNIFICANCE is that, once all the self-imposed scope caps are taken at face value, the demonstrated benefit to any concrete stakeholder is small and largely unvalidated. (1) The headline "three structurally distinct domains" generalization is protocol/demonstration, not result: one domain is the authors' own prior catalogue (self-disclosed as internal-vocabulary-coherence, not external transfer); one is a 5,189-parameter toy EGNN; the third (relational optimisers) is a paper exercise whose four MRs the authors admit are "not de-novo discoveries" and merely correspond to already-published query-equivalence identities. (2) The only executable head-to-head against a real SOTA baseline (GenMorph) is LOST (26 vs 40 kills, McNemar p=0.0043), and the contribution is then relabeled to per-block/cost-axis/complementarity. (3) Every empirical cohort that could establish practitioner value is small and self-disclosed as underpowered (case study n=1 model / 20 hand-constructed-to-favor-coverage mutations; DeepCrime pilot n=5, p=0.5; cross-codebase pilot n=3/77), and the systematization/auditability value that is the actual claimed benefit is supported only by LLM-panel kappa with no human raters and no adoption evidence. The theory contributions are real but modest by the authors' own characterization ("intentionally modest," "well-formedness guarantee"). Because so much of the would-be significance is explicitly deferred to committed future work, the paper currently lands at borderline-low for TOSEM's significance bar: the ideas matter, but the evidence that anyone benefits substantially does not yet exist in the manuscript. Most concerns are honestly bounded by the paper, which raises the floor; but bounded-and-deferred is still deferred, and significance cannot be scored on promised work.

findings.issue: The central transferability/generalization claim — that NOETHER works across 'three structurally distinct domains' — is a protocol/demonstration of derivability, not a result that establishes value to a population of users. The reactor domain is the authors' OWN prior catalogue (self-disclosed: 'best read as a test of internal vocabulary coherence ... not external transfer of tacit knowledge from an independent reactor-physics team'); the equivariant-ML domain is a single 5,189-parameter toy EGNN; and the relational-optimiser domain produces four MRs that 'are not de-novo MR discovery (these identities are already in the published optimiser-equivalence literature).' None of the three demonstrates that NOETHER lets a real team identify MRs they could not otherwise identify.
findings.evidence: §subsec:third-domain: 'NOETHER's contribution on A_rel is not de-novo MR discovery (these identities are already in the published optimiser-equivalence literature) but the uniform algebraic warrant.' §subsec:reactor-mapping: 'the underlying PWR-MR corpus (supplementary S2) is the authors' own catalogue, not an external corpus ... This is internal consistency under a uniform algebraic structure, not external transfer.' C4: 'We demonstrate structural transferability at the algebra-skeleton level (not cross-domain empirical superiority).'
findings.suggested_fix: Add at least one genuine external-transfer instance: apply the frozen blocks to an MR corpus or program family authored by an independent team (the paper itself names PARCS V&V / IAEA-TECDOC as the missing test) and report whether NOETHER recovers MRs not in that team's catalogue. Until then, downgrade the abstract/conclusion language from 'transferability ... across three structurally distinct domains' to 'derivability re-demonstrated on three algebra skeletons, two of which are exercises against already-published or own-authored MR sets,' so significance is not overstated.

findings.issue: The single executable head-to-head against a real automated SOTA baseline is LOST in aggregate (Set N 26 vs Set G 40 kills, McNemar p=0.0043). For a TOSEM reader asking 'who benefits and by how much,' the one head-to-head that uses a neutral, externally-defined defect substrate shows the proposed method underperforming the GP baseline on detection. The paper salvages significance by reframing to per-block complementarity and a cost-axis argument, but this is a substantial blow to practitioner-facing significance that the per-block reading only partially offsets.
findings.evidence: §subsec:pooled-headtohead: 'On the algebra-disrupting D1 stratum at GenMorph's published 30-min GAssert budget, Set N is dominated by Set G in the aggregate (McNemar exact two-sided p = 0.0043 pooled ...).' Table tab:algebra-rich-pooled pooled row: Set N 26, Set G 40, Δ = -14.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the cost-axis advantage quantitative and decision-relevant (e.g., MRs/hour and total wall-clock to reach a target kill rate including human time), and add the union-coverage value proposition explicitly (N+G union vs G alone) as the practitioner takeaway. If the cost/complementarity argument is the real significance, foreground it with numbers rather than letting a lost detection head-to-head stand as the dominant impression.

findings.issue: The empirical evidence that the framework's derived MRs catch faults rests on cohorts too small and too construct-controlled to support generalization to any real target population, and the paper itself says so. The case study is one model, 20 mutations hand-constructed to put one defect category per block (so the 5/5 cat-iv 'win' is construct-validity-controlled by design); the real-fault DeepCrime pilot is n=5 with McNemar p=0.500 (not significant). This caps how much the significance claim ('benefits practitioners testing oracle-free systems') can actually be believed from the data presented.
findings.evidence: §subsec:case-study: 'the comparison's denominator (20 mutations, one model) is too small.' Construct-validity caveat: 'cat-(iv) was selected because it targets the T* block that rho_train-rev alone covers. The 5/5 unique-detection result therefore exhibits construct validity ... not NOETHER's superiority on a defect distribution sampled neutrally.' §subsec:deepcrime-pilot: 'two-sided exact p = 0.500 ... the pilot is therefore underpowered for an inferential conclusion at alpha = 0.05.'
findings.suggested_fix: Execute the already-fully-specified real-bug protocol (e3nn / PyTorch Geometric mined faults, §para:real-bug-protocol) and the comparative-evaluation protocol (DeepCrime MNIST/CIFAR-10, GenMorph 23-method benchmark) before claiming practitioner significance. The protocols are written but not run; significance for TOSEM should rest on executed neutral-substrate results, not on committed future work.

findings.issue: The PRIMARY significance metric (EQ1 binary operator-block coverage) is constructed so that NOETHER essentially cannot lose: a block counts as covered if the paper 'derives at least one explicit MR class' in it, while the cross-domain column that shows NOETHER covering 6 blocks vs experts' 1 is measured on held-out numerical libraries the authors selected, not on the same artefacts as the expert sets. The expert-industrial vs NOETHER-industrial columns are in fact identical (both cover only O_le). So the load-bearing 'broader design space' claim is carried by a column (NOETHER cross-domain) measured on different, favorably-chosen subjects. This inflates the apparent significance of the coverage advantage.
findings.evidence: Table tab:expert-noether-binary-coverage: Expert industrial and NOETHER industrial columns are identical (only O_le = 1); the breadth comes from 'NOETHER cross-domain' (6 blocks), which the caption ties to 'held-out numpy.linalg and numpy.fft subjects in supplementary S12' — different artefacts from the SACOS/SPARK/LOCUST expert sets. Text: 'NOETHER ... covers a broader operator-block design space than the expert industrial corpora available to us.'
findings.suggested_fix: Report block coverage of NOETHER and the expert sets on the SAME artefacts (apply NOETHER's derivation to SACOS/SPARK/LOCUST governing equations and count which blocks become executable on those interfaces), so the breadth comparison is apples-to-apples rather than NOETHER-on-favorable-libraries vs experts-on-industrial-code. Acknowledge in-text that the industrial-vs-industrial columns are currently tied at one block.

findings.issue: The claimed practitioner benefit is largely systematization/auditability (deduplication, canonical placement, origin/boundary explanations), yet the only inter-rater evidence that these classifications are usable/reproducible comes from LLM panels that share training data, with no human raters. Significance for 'auditable by maintainers' is therefore asserted but not demonstrated with the relevant population (human engineers). The paper self-discloses this, which bounds the concern.
findings.evidence: §sec:threats-limitations construct validity: 'the inter-rater agreement figures (kappa = 0.857 ... and kappa = 1.000 ...) are drawn from rater panels composed entirely of large language models ... should be read as consistency among similarly-trained but non-coordinated raters rather than as independent human-level verification ... a human inter-rater kappa study is committed as follow-up rather than claimed in this paper.'
findings.suggested_fix: Run a small human inter-rater study (2-3 domain engineers classifying a sample of MRs into the eight blocks) to substantiate the auditability/reproducibility value proposition that underpins the framework's practical significance; even n=2 raters on ~20 items would convert an asserted benefit into a demonstrated one.

findings.issue: The theoretical contributions that carry significance are characterized by the authors as deliberately modest, which is appropriate but limits the 'how much' of who-benefits. Theorem 1 is a by-construction well-formedness guarantee, not evidence the block list is complete or that derived MRs are better; the Invariance-Blindness Theorem is scoped to two blocks (G, T*) and the linear fault class. A TOSEM reader weighing significance should note the strongest, most general claim (absolute completeness) is the one shown FALSE, and the surviving positive theory is narrow.
findings.evidence: C2a: 'This result is intentionally modest. It is a well-formedness guarantee for the downstream construction, not evidence that the upstream block list is complete and not evidence of fault-detection superiority.' C2c: Invariance-Blindness holds 'for the symmetry (G) and self-adjoint (T*) blocks ... within the linear operator-implementation fault class.'
findings.suggested_fix: No change needed for honesty (the scoping is exemplary), but to raise significance, either extend the Invariance-Blindness characterization beyond {G, T*} / linear faults to one more block, or make the practical payoff of the closure guarantee concrete (e.g., show a tool that uses closure to guarantee no derivable MR class is dropped, with a measured benefit over an ad-hoc enumeration).

reviews.summary: NOETHER_paper_arxiv.tex is a technically rich, carefully hedged paper, but its presentation does not meet the TOSEM bar. The dominant problem is length and density: the arxiv PDF is 80 pages, with 21 tables, 1 figure, 36 subsubsections, and 134 named \paragraph headers, plus 77 pointers into supplementary material S1-S12. The result is a manuscript whose load-bearing claims (Theorem 1 closure, the Invariance-Blindness Theorem, the L*-blindness prediction, EQ1-EQ3 coverage) are buried under exhaustive sub-strata, scope caveats, and process bookkeeping. Several genuine notation and consistency defects compound the navigation problem: the time-reversal block is written with three different symbols; the EQ1/EQ3 results tables introduce a "Conservation" block that is not one of the eight formally defined blocks; and the body carries heavy pre-registration / "committed to git" / "subsequent revisions of this paper" process narrative that belongs in a response letter, not a results paper. Compilation is clean (no undefined \ref, no overfull >50pt, abstract is 317 words and stand-alone), and the contribution boundary boxes are commendably honest, so the core is fixable, but the paper as presented would exhaust and lose a TOSEM reader. Substantial restructuring and compression are required before it reads as a publishable method paper rather than a technical report. Score 2 (poor, below borderline) on presentation specifically.

findings.issue: The arxiv PDF is 80 pages (confirmed: log reports 'Output written ... (80 pages)'), far beyond TOSEM method-paper norms (~35-45 pages). Structural census: 21 \begin{table}, 36 \subsubsection, 134 \paragraph{...} named headers, 4 'Boundary of contribution' tcolorboxes, and 77 distinct pointers to supplementary S1-S12. The Results/Discussion section alone (sec:results-discussion) spans roughly lines 1084-2700 with nested sub-results, two-stratum tables, per-block tables, pooled tables, sensitivity reruns, and pilots. A reader cannot locate or hold the load-bearing claims; the primary EQ1-EQ3 evidence is interleaved with secondary executability checks, a DeepCrime pilot, a Path A METRIC+ head-to-head, an LLM ensemble, and an IBT empirical appendix.
findings.evidence: NOETHER_paper_arxiv.log: 'Output written on NOETHER_paper_arxiv.pdf (80 pages, 1118818 bytes).' Counts via parse: tables=21, paragraph-headers=134, subsubsections=36, supplementary-pointers=77.
findings.suggested_fix: Cut to TOSEM length by moving the secondary empirical apparatus (the §5.2 case study + DeepCrime pilot, the full §5.4 PIT head-to-head sub-tables, the §5.6 METRIC+ Path A execution, the §5.7 IBT empirical E1-E3) into a clearly-signposted online appendix, retaining one summary table each in the body. Collapse the 134 \paragraph headers; a body with 3-8 results subsections is the target. Keep Theorem 1, the IBT, the PWR negative result, and EQ1-EQ3 coverage as the spine.

findings.issue: The time-reversal block is denoted by three inconsistent symbols for the same object: \mathcal{T}^{*} (~23 uses, including the formal decomposition tuple in Def at L466 and Hypothesis 1 at L478), \mathcal{T}^{*}_{\mathrm{rev}} (~11 uses), and \mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{rev}}^{*} (~6 uses). The architecture figure (L199) lists the block as \mathcal{T}^{*}_{\mathrm{rev}} while the canonical decomposition definition (L466) names it \mathcal{T}^{*}, so the figure and the definition it summarises disagree.
findings.evidence: L466: '\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_P) = (G, O_{\le}, T^{*}, \mathcal{T}^{*}, \mathcal{L}^{*}, ...)'; L199 figure node lists '\mathcal{T}^{*}_{\mathrm{rev}}'; PWR proof Appendix C.6 uses '\mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{rev}}^{*}'. Counts: T^{*}_{rev}=11, T_{rev}^{*}=6, bare \mathcal{T}^{*}=23.
findings.suggested_fix: Choose one canonical symbol (e.g. \mathcal{T}^{*}_{\mathrm{rev}}) and apply it everywhere, including the §3.1 tuple, Hypothesis 1, Fig. 1, the per-block cost table, the PIT-block matrix, and the Appendix C.6 proof.

findings.section: §5.1 Tables EQ1 & EQ3 (L1113-1124, L1176-1198); §6 held-out paragraph (L2771)
findings.issue: The load-bearing primary-evidence tables introduce a 'Conservation' block row that is not among the eight blocks formally defined in §3.1 (G, O_{\le}, T^{*}, time-reversal, L^{*}, D^{*}, E^{*}, B^{*}_{rel}). The transferability paragraph similarly enumerates 'six blocks each (G, T^{*}, O_{\le}, L^{*}, E^{*}, and a conservation invariant)'. In the framework, conservation/invariance is part of the G block (P1 'conservation/invariance' maps to m_inv in G per Table tab:refinement), so the tables present an undefined ninth label as if it were a separate block, contradicting the eight-block taxonomy that the whole paper's closure argument rests on.
findings.evidence: Table EQ1 row: 'Conservation & 0 & 0 & 1'; Table EQ3 row: 'Conservation & Reactor balance equations; FFT/Parseval checks ...'; L2771: 'populate six blocks each ($G$, $T^{*}$, $O_{\le}$, $\mathcal{L}^{*}$, $\mathcal{E}^{*}$, and a conservation invariant)'. §3.1 (L466) defines exactly eight blocks, none named 'Conservation'.
findings.suggested_fix: Relabel the 'Conservation' rows to the canonical G block (or to whichever defined block holds conservation invariants), or add one explicit sentence in §3.1 stating that conservation invariants are realised within the G block, so the tables do not name an undefined block.

findings.issue: The body carries extensive research-process / pre-registration / version-tracking narrative that belongs in a response letter or replication note, not the manuscript proper. 'Pre-register(ed/ration)' appears ~16 times in-body; 'committed to git', 'git timestamp chain', 'SHA-256 ... deposited' appear as prose; 'committed as follow-up' / 'committed future work' appears 19 times; and one sentence frames the paper as a living document: 'leaving only the result population to subsequent revisions of this paper.' This reads as process bookkeeping and over-hedges the contribution, harming readability for a TOSEM audience.
findings.evidence: L1357: 'leaving only the result population to subsequent revisions of this paper.' L1496/L1617/L2280: 'committed to git ... before the per-MR kill-count files' / 'git timestamp chain (criterion -> inscope filter -> Set N derivation -> ...)'. 19 occurrences of 'committed as follow-up'.
findings.suggested_fix: Move pre-registration provenance and git-timestamp evidence to the artifact/replication appendix; reduce 'committed as follow-up' to a single consolidated future-work paragraph; delete the 'subsequent revisions of this paper' framing (a results paper presents results, not a revision roadmap).

findings.issue: Theorem cross-references mix hard-coded numbers with \ref. The closure theorem is cited as Theorem~\ref{thm:closure} 48 times but once as bare 'Theorem~1' (L257). The decidability theorem is Theorem~\ref{thm:decidable} 17 times but appears hard-coded as 'Theorem 2'/'Theorem~2' 4 times (e.g. proof heading 'Theorem 2 (Decidability), full proof', and 'Theorem~2 was originally stated'). With acmart auto-numbering this risks the printed number drifting from the hardcoded text if a theorem is added.
findings.evidence: L257: 'Theorem~1 proves a no-drop closure invariant'; L2946 heading: 'Theorem 2 (Decidability), full proof'; L648: 'the regime under which Theorem~2 was originally stated'.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace all hard-coded 'Theorem 1' / 'Theorem 2' with \ref{thm:closure} / \ref{thm:decidable} (keeping the distinct unnumbered conjecture Theorem 1' as the deliberately-primed name).

findings.issue: Spelling is predominantly British (-ise: characterise/formalise/generalise/systematise; 'characterisation' x6) but several American forms are mixed in prose: 'characterization' (L259, L2750), 'realization' (L386), 'behavior' (L1082), 'organizing' (L2759). Per the project's own consistency rule, one convention must be chosen throughout.
findings.evidence: L259: 'a falsifiable, non-tautological characterization'; L2750: 'the kernel characterization of Theorem'; L386: 'a downstream realization'; L1082: 'expected category-specific behavior'; vs 6 British 'characterisation' elsewhere.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalise to British -ise/-isation throughout (change characterization->characterisation, realization->realisation, behavior->behaviour, organizing->organising). Exclude LaTeX command names (itemize, footnotesize, scriptsize) which are not prose.

findings.issue: Two LaTeX font-shape warnings indicate small-caps and italic shapes are undefined for the body font (T1/zi4), so \textsc{} / italic small-caps may silently fall back. Cosmetic but worth resolving for camera-ready typographic fidelity.
findings.evidence: NOETHER_paper_arxiv.log: 'LaTeX Font Warning: Font shape `T1/zi4/m/sc' undefined' and '`T1/zi4/m/it' undefined'. (No undefined \ref or \cite, and no Overfull \hbox > 50pt — those are clean.)
findings.suggested_fix: Load a font package providing the missing shapes or avoid \scshape on the affected font; verify the warnings clear on recompile.

verified.issue: The Invariance-Blindness Theorem is the paper's designated non-tautological theoretical contribution (C2c), but as stated it is near-circular. Definition (Faithfulness) reads: a finite witness set is faithful iff ker(ρ_{ι,s})=C(T_s). Theorem IBT then concludes ker(ρ_{ι,s})=C(T_s)=C(T_s) 'given faithful witnesses.' The conclusion is literally the assumption. The proof's ⊆ direction is one line that simply invokes the faithfulness definition. All genuine mathematical content is in Lemma (Reachability of faithfulness) — that a finite faithful witness set EXISTS — which the paper itself flags ('Lemma is the crux: tightness is not tautological but follows from finite fault-dimensionality').
verified.evidence: Def: 'A finite witness set W^test_s is faithful iff ker(ρ_{ι,s})=C(T_s)'. Theorem: '...let the test witnesses be faithful (Definition...). Then ker(ρ_{ι,s})=C(T_s)=...'. Proof ⊆: 'If L∈ker then E_s(L;w)=0 on W^test_s; by faithfulness ... ker(ρ_{ι,s})=C(T_s), so L∈C(T_s).'
verified.suggested_fix: Restate the theorem so the load-bearing claim is the Reachability Lemma's conclusion (a finite executable witness set attains the exact blind set C(T_s)), making faithfulness a proven property rather than a hypothesis whose statement coincides with the conclusion. Either fold the lemma into the theorem as its main clause, or drop 'faithful' as a hypothesis and conclude existence of a finite W^test with ker=C(T_s). As written, the theorem cannot be cited as 'falsifiable, non-tautological' (its abstract/intro framing) without this restructuring.

Faithfulness (L59-65) literally states ker(rho)=C(T_s); Theorem IBT (L86-96) takes faithfulness as hypothesis and concludes ker(rho)=C(T_s); and the proof's ⊆ direction (L101-103) is one line invoking the definition. So the narrow logical observation is correct, not a misread. BUT the finding is NOT an un-addressed soundness defect, because the paper has already self-disclosed and correctly bounded exactly this point. (1) The Lemma-crux remark (L82-84): 'Lemma is the crux: tightness is not tautological but follows from finite fault-dimensionality.' The paper explicitly says the trivial part is trivial and locates the real content in the Reachability Lemma (a FINITE faithful witness set EXISTS — proved via finite-dimensionality of the dual, L67-80) plus the kernel identification C(T_s)={L: P_L preserves T_s}. verified.section: §3.3.3 Theorem 2 (Decidability) + Table (Per-block invariant-extraction cost); also Abstract/Intro/Conclusion 'polynomial-time'
verified.issue: The contribution is repeatedly headlined as 'polynomial-time decidability of CONSTRUCT-MP.' The proven bound is O(n·max_i t_i·log n) where n = number of GENERATORS, but the per-generator cost for the symmetry block is t_i=O(|G|^2) for finite groups. |G| is exponential in n for many finitely generated groups (e.g. (Z_2)^k has |G|=2^k from k generators). So the bound is polynomial in (n, |G|, d, K), i.e. in output/group size, not in input size — the standard meaning of 'polynomial-time' for a decidability claim. The Lie-group O(d_G^2) and infinite-discrete truncation O(K^2) prose correctly scopes this, but the unqualified term propagates to the abstract, the five-contribution list, the boundary boxes, and the conclusion.
verified.evidence: Theorem 2: 'O(n·max_i t_i·log n)'. Cost table first row: 'finite group | O(|G|^2) (group-orbit fixed-point)'. Prose: 'The asymptotic bound is therefore not the binding constraint in either instantiation' (i.e. finite small |G| in the instances), but Conclusion box still asserts '(ii) polynomial-time decidability under finite generating-set assumption.'
verified.suggested_fix: Qualify every headline occurrence to 'polynomial in the generating-set and group/output size' or 'fixed-parameter / output-polynomial,' and state explicitly in Theorem 2 that t_i may be exponential in n for finite groups whose order is exponential in their generator count. confirmed.section: §3.3.3 Theorem 2 (Decidability) + Table (Per-block invariant-extraction cost); also Abstract/Intro/Conclusion 'polynomial-time'
confirmed.issue: The contribution is repeatedly headlined as 'polynomial-time decidability of CONSTRUCT-MP.' The proven bound is O(n·max_i t_i·log n) where n = number of GENERATORS, but the per-generator cost for the symmetry block is t_i=O(|G|^2) for finite groups. |G| is exponential in n for many finitely generated groups (e.g. (Z_2)^k has |G|=2^k from k generators). So the bound is polynomial in (n, |G|, d, K), i.e. in output/group size, not in input size — the standard meaning of 'polynomial-time' for a decidability claim. The Lie-group O(d_G^2) and infinite-discrete truncation O(K^2) prose correctly scopes this, but the unqualified term propagates to the abstract, the five-contribution list, the boundary boxes, and the conclusion.

eic.rationale: The paper's load-bearing theoretical contribution is genuine and TOSEM-shaped: constructive derivation of a MetaPattern layer from a program-induced operator algebra, with a closure theorem, a (scoped) decidability result, a falsified absolute-completeness conjecture on a real safety algebra, and the Invariance-Blindness Theorem characterizing the detection kernel as the commutant of structure-preserving faults. All four deep-research angles independently rate venue fit 3-4 and agree the IBT + negative-completeness + constructive-closure package has no clear MT precedent, so novelty (68) and the theory side of soundness hold up. The score is pulled down by what adversarial verification CONFIRMED as real and still-live, not by the many findings it overturned. I discounted the large set of significance/novelty 'overclaim' findings that verification marked not-real (confidence 4-5) because the manuscript already self-discloses and scopes them (reactor self-catalogue, toy EGNN, lost GenMorph head-to-head reframed to cost/coverage, by-construction Theorem 1, IBT near-circularity bounded by the Reachability Lemma); the time-reversal symbol 'inconsistency' was verified false; and the Conservation-block issue, flagged real, now has an explicit reconciliation at L469 in the live file. What survives is concentrated and serious: a reproducible data contradiction (Set L 0.40 vs SSOT 0.20, verified this session in table4.json, propagated into the submission tex), two missing cited artifacts, an inter-rater figure that reports the vacuous LLM-LLM kappa and hides the imperfect human-validation kappa, an 80-page manuscript ~3x the TOSEM soft cap (LEN-01 FAIL, a return-without-review trigger), an unqualified polynomial-time claim, several missing closest-cousin citations, and 72% format/process compliance. These are overwhelmingly fixable without new science: the integrity and artifact items are hours of work, and even the length blocker is condensation rather than re-experimentation. Hence Major Revision, not Reject: strong, defensible core; presentation (38) and a cluster of confirmed integrity/reproducibility defects make it not submission-ready today. Acceptance probability as-is (~22%) reflects that the length and data-contradiction blockers would likely draw a return-without-review or a reproducibility-driven reject before the theory is fully credited; clearing the P0/P1 roadmap items would plausibly move this into the 45-55% range for a revised resubmission.
